# mimir

[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/mimir-agent.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/mimir-agent/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](./LICENSE)

A memory-centric agent harness built on [deepagents](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents)
(LangGraph). Install: `pip install mimir-agent`.

mimir wraps an LLM agent loop with the surrounding apparatus a long-running
agent needs to operate over time, across channels, and across sessions:
persistent memory (the in-process `mimir.saga` backend), a tool-and-skill registry, scheduled
ticks for autonomous work, message bridges (Discord / Slack / Bluesky / web /
benchmark stdout), and a feedback-loop / homeostat layer that keeps the
agent regulated as it accumulates state.

The name is from Norse myth — Mímir, the keeper of memory and counsel.

## What it gives you

- **A real memory backend.** Every turn is recorded; significant
  observations consolidate into structured atoms with embedding +
  triple representations; retrieval at the start of each turn pulls
  relevant prior context into the prompt automatically.
- **Skills, not just tools.** Skills are markdown files an agent
  loads on demand to learn a workflow (the librarian protocol, the
  five-whys debugging skill, the reflection skill, etc.) — decision-
  framework and failure-mode docs that the tool description alone
  can't carry.
- **Scheduled work.** Cron-backed scheduler fires per-channel ticks
  (heartbeat, reflection, custom). The §12.4 homeostat suppresses
  ticks when the plan window saturates or cost-rate trips.
- **Multi-channel bridges.** Discord, Slack, Bluesky, web chat,
  benchmark stdout. The agent has one identity across channels;
  `state/identities.yaml` resolves platform aliases to canonical
  names.
- **Reflection + double-loop learning.** Weekly reflection skill
  audits behavior + memory architecture, drafts proposals into
  `state/proposed-changes.md`, and (via the §12.2 applied-proposals
  audit) closes the loop on whether merged changes actually helped.
- **Predictions and calibration.** Agent writes structured
  predictions about future outcomes; CLI tracks them; weekly review
  compares predicted vs measured. Single source of operational
  calibration data.

## Repository layout

```
mimir/                              # the agent harness — top-level package
mimir/saga/                         # in-process memory backend (runtime)
benchmarks/longmemeval_via_mimir/   # integration bench against LongMemEval
benchmarks/saga/                    # bench shell — separate workspace package, imported by the longmemeval runners
tests/                              # pytest suite
docs/                               # architectural notes (public) + internal/ (process docs)
SPEC.md                             # detailed design doc
FEEDBACK-LOOPS.md                   # mapping of every feedback loop in the system
```

The runtime memory backend lives at `mimir/saga/` and is part of the
`mimir-agent` package. The `saga` workspace package at `benchmarks/saga/`
is a separate bench shell that the LongMemEval runners under
`benchmarks/longmemeval_via_mimir/` import as
`saga.benchmarks.longmemeval.*`.

## Quickstart

Requires Python 3.11+.

### Install from PyPI

```bash
pip install "mimir-agent[anthropic]"   # pick the model-provider extra(s) you'll use

# Set up an agent home (creates dirs, seeds skills, generates API keys)
mimir setup --home ~/mimir-home

# Configure auth — pick one
#   API key:                     edit ~/mimir-home/.env, set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
#   Anthropic Max plan (free):   one extra install step — see "Claude Max plan" below
#   Gateway:                     set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
#   Non-Anthropic Anthropic-compat (Minimax, Kimi, …): see "Alternative providers"

# Optional but recommended for saga's embeddings:
#   set OPENAI_API_KEY in ~/mimir-home/.env

# Run
mimir run --home ~/mimir-home
```

Available extras (combine in one install command — e.g. `pip install
"mimir-agent[anthropic,discord,slack,mcp]"`):

| Extra | Pulls |
|---|---|
| `anthropic`, `openai`, `codex-plus` | model adapter packages (`codex-plus` = ChatGPT Plus / Pro Codex subscription via the OAuth-backed gateway) |
| `discord`, `slack` | bridge runtimes |
| `mcp` | Model Context Protocol client |

For **Claude Max** (the subprocess provider via `langchain-claude-code`),
that package is currently a git-pinned fork — PyPI rejects published
packages that declare direct `git+` URLs, so it isn't an extra. Install
the fork as a separate step after `mimir-agent`:

```bash
pip install mimir-agent[anthropic]
pip install "langchain-claude-code @ git+https://github.com/jasoncarreira/langchain-claude-code@f7af15b613d1e016437740f739321316730cdd39"
claude setup-token   # OAuth dance — once per host
```

This works around upstream PRs (#2 / #4 / #6) that haven't merged yet.
Once they land + a release is cut, the second `pip install` collapses
back into a `[claude-code]` extra. Tracked in mimir-repo issue #268.

### Or clone for development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jasoncarreira/mimir.git
cd mimir
uv sync --extra dev
# For the Claude Code subprocess path, also:
# uv pip install "langchain-claude-code @ git+https://github.com/jasoncarreira/langchain-claude-code@f7af15b613d1e016437740f739321316730cdd39"

uv run mimir setup --home ~/mimir-home
uv run mimir run --home ~/mimir-home
```

`mimir setup` activates four recurring tasks out of the box: hourly
heartbeat, weekly reflection, weekly saga consolidation, weekly
behavioral introspection report. All gated by the homeostat so a
saturated plan window doesn't blow through your quota.

See `.env.example` for every environment variable mimir reads.

## Alternative providers (Minimax, Kimi, …)

`MIMIR_MODEL_SPEC` picks the model and provider. Forms:

- `claude-code:<model>` — Max OAuth subprocess (default, free under Max plan).
- `anthropic:<model>` — direct Anthropic API (paid credit).
- `openai:<model>` — direct OpenAI.

Reasoning-token model families that expose an **Anthropic-compat
endpoint** (Minimax, Moonshot Kimi) ride the `anthropic:` provider with
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` overridden:

```bash
# Minimax via Anthropic-compat
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<minimax-key>
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.minimax.io/anthropic
MIMIR_MODEL_SPEC=anthropic:MiniMax-M2.7
```

```bash
# Moonshot Kimi via Anthropic-compat
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<moonshot-key>
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.moonshot.ai/anthropic
MIMIR_MODEL_SPEC=anthropic:kimi-k2-0905-preview
```

Prefer Anthropic-compat over OpenAI-compat for these providers when both
are offered: the provider converts reasoning to proper Anthropic-shape
`thinking` content blocks server-side. The OAI-compat path returns the
same model's reasoning as inline `<think>...</think>` tags in the
content string — a less structured response that mimir would have to
parse out before it could be cleanly logged + suppressed.

Note: overriding `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` also affects any other consumer
in the same process (e.g., the `claude` CLI subprocess that saga's
`claude_code` provider spawns). If you set this, configure saga.toml's
`[llm]` to route through the same alternate provider rather than
falling back to `claude_code` — see
[`saga/saga.example.toml`](./saga/saga.example.toml) for the
provider options + per-section documentation.

## Scheduler timezone

`scheduler.yaml` cron expressions are interpreted in UTC by default —
e.g., `cron: "0 8 * * *"` means 08:00 UTC, not 08:00 in your local
time. Set `MIMIR_SCHEDULER_TZ` to a IANA zone to author crons in
local wall-clock time (DST-aware via system tzdata):

```bash
MIMIR_SCHEDULER_TZ=America/New_York   # ET-shaped crons
```

Affects every cron in the agent home: `scheduler.yaml` LLM-tick jobs,
auto-installed `saga-consolidate` and `introspection-report`,
commitments-due-check, and every poller from
`.claude/skills/*/pollers.json`. Invalid zone names fall back to UTC
with a logged warning rather than crashing the scheduler.

## Development

Optional extras:

| Extra | Pulls | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `[dev]` | pytest + bridges + Anthropic / OpenAI / Codex Plus adapters + faiss | Default for contributors — covers the agent core, saga, bridges. Claude-code-specific tests skip cleanly via `pytest.importorskip`. |
| `[anthropic]` / `[openai]` / `[codex-plus]` | Single model adapter | Runtime install with one model path. |

Developers on the Claude Code subprocess path install the
git-pinned fork as a separate step (same reasoning as the runtime
Claude Max path above):

```bash
uv sync --extra dev
uv pip install "langchain-claude-code @ git+https://github.com/jasoncarreira/langchain-claude-code@f7af15b613d1e016437740f739321316730cdd39"
```

```bash
# Tests — minimal toolchain (claude-code-specific tests will skip)
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"
uv run pytest                                       # 600+ tests
uv run pytest --ignore=tests/test_bench_via_mimir.py  # skip the slow integration test

# Tests — full toolchain (claude-code-specific tests will run)
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"
uv pip install "langchain-claude-code @ git+https://github.com/jasoncarreira/langchain-claude-code@f7af15b613d1e016437740f739321316730cdd39"
uv run pytest
```

The bench harness is in `benchmarks/longmemeval_via_mimir/`. See
that directory's README for running an A/B of two saga configs and
scoring with the gpt-4o judge.

## Reading order

If you're orienting yourself in the codebase:

1. **[SPEC.md](./SPEC.md)** — what mimir is, the design choices
2. **[FEEDBACK-LOOPS.md](./FEEDBACK-LOOPS.md)** — the regulatory
   architecture (mapped to Beer's Viable System Model)
3. **[mimir/saga/\_\_init\_\_.py](./mimir/saga/__init__.py)** — memory
   backend operation surface (the module docstring is the public-API
   reference)
4. **[docs/](./docs/)** — additional architectural notes (`docs/internal/`
   holds historical process docs that may help when archeology is needed
   but aren't part of the public contract)

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE). Copyright © 2026 Jason Carreira.

## Contributing & security

- [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) — how to file issues and PRs
- [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) — vulnerability disclosure + threat-model posture
- [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md) — release notes

# Contributing to mimir

Thanks for your interest. mimir is an early-stage open-source project; the
contribution flow is still maturing. Below is what works today.

## Quick path

1. Open a GitHub issue describing the bug or proposal before you start a
   substantial change. Small fixes (typos, obvious bugs, tightening a
   docstring) can go straight to a PR.
2. Fork, branch off `main`, push, open a PR. Reference the issue.
3. Run `uv run pytest` locally — CI is currently best-effort while the repo
   moves to public Actions minutes.
4. Sign your commits if you can; not required.

## What kind of change is in scope

In scope:

- Bug fixes
- Documentation improvements
- New skills (markdown-only, additive)
- New optional bridges (Discord/Slack-style adapters)
- New optional model providers
- Tests, especially regression tests for failures observed in the field

Less likely to be accepted without prior discussion:

- Changes to the memory backend's on-disk schema (touches saga)
- Changes to the agent loop's prompt-construction order (affects every
  deployment's prompt cache)
- Replacing a dependency with a different one for taste reasons

If you're unsure, open an issue first.

## Code style

- Python 3.11+
- Prefer existing patterns over introducing new abstractions
- `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of new modules
- Type hints on public functions; `from typing import Optional` style is fine
- Tests live under `tests/`; one file per module under test, matching name
- No emoji in code or commit messages unless an existing file already uses them

## Tests

```bash
uv sync
uv run pytest                                          # full suite
uv run pytest tests/test_specific_module.py            # one file
uv run pytest --ignore=tests/test_bench_via_mimir.py   # skip slow integration
```

If your change touches the agent loop, run the bench harness before opening
the PR — see `benchmarks/longmemeval_via_mimir/README.md`. Memory-backend
changes (`mimir/saga/`) are covered by `tests/test_saga_*` in the main
test suite — no separate `cd` is needed.

## Reviewing

PRs need one approving review before merge. The bar is "does this make the
system better and not regress anything else." Drive-by suggestions are fine
in comments; blocking changes should map to the contribution-scope guidance
above.

## Security

For vulnerabilities, see [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md). Do not open public
issues for security concerns.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: feedback: classify *_gave_up poller events as negative algedonic signals (chainlink #299)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Summary
This change is the right generalization for chainlink #299: moving event classification behind a shared `classify()` helper avoids per-poller table churn while making `*_gave_up` events surface uniformly across recent-feedback rendering, run detection, escalation counting, and the CLI validator. The renderer/test additions are also pointed at the real operator-visible behavior, not just the helper in isolation.

## Observations
- `mimir/feedback/rules.py`: exact-match-first before the suffix convention is the right precedence rule; it preserves the canonical table as the source of truth while still giving future pollers a zero-config negative surface for exhausted retries.
- `mimir/feedback/renderers.py`: preferring `repo#number` over `url` in the one-line render is a good choice for prompt compactness, and reusing `_sanitize_field()` keeps the GitHub-target path aligned with the existing sanitization rule from #224.
- `tests/test_feedback.py`: the end-to-end assertion is the load-bearing test here. It proves the new convention actually reaches the negative algedonic block instead of only unit-testing the helper.

## Test coverage note
The PR description reports `test_feedback.py` and `test_cli.py` green. CI is still running on the full matrix as I submit this review, but the changed surfaces and targeted tests look appropriate for the behavior being added.

## Non-blocking suggestions
None.

payload.title: feat(skills): ship optional-skills in the wheel so the CLI can install them on pip installs (chainlink #299)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body: test review submission from mimir

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Summary
This looks right. The PR moves optional skills under `mimir/optional-skills/`, updates the runtime resolvers to look there, and adds the wheel include so `mimir skills install` / `list-optional` work from pip installs instead of only from source checkouts.

I also like the CI shape: keeping the main suite on `tests/` while running each optional-skill test tree in its own pytest process is the right response to the shared `poller.py` / `tests.conftest` module-name collisions.

## Observations
- `pyproject.toml` now explicitly includes `mimir/optional-skills/**/*` in the wheel build allowlist, which is the load-bearing packaging fix.
- `mimir/skill_install.py` and `mimir/scaffold_docker.py` both now resolve bundled optional skills from under the package, so the source layout and installed-wheel layout match.
- CI is green on both supported Python versions plus skill-conformance, so the packaging/layout change appears to be covered end-to-end.

## Test coverage
The dedicated per-skill pytest loop is a solid addition here. It exercises the moved trees without reintroducing the known import-path collision that would happen if all optional-skill tests were run in one interpreter.

No blocking issues from me.

payload.title: feat(optional-skills): vendor github-ci-watch poller into mimir source

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
Summary:
This vendors the last missing GitHub poller skill into `optional-skills/` and fixes the carried-over run-URL bug at the same time. The implementation is straightforward, the event contract is clear, and the tests cover the load-bearing behavior: only new completed failures emit, seen-set dedup works, and the emitted URL now comes from the correct `gh run list --json` field.

Observations:
- `poller.py` cleanly follows the poller contract: silence on green, one JSONL event per new broken run, and persistent seen-state capped to prevent unbounded growth.
- The latent `url` vs `htmlUrl` bug is fixed in the right place and locked with an assertion in `test_emits_only_new_completed_failures`.
- `pollers.json` passes the right env vars for this shape (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_REPOS`, `STATE_DIR`).
- `SKILL.md` is useful and fills the documentation gap from the operator-local copy.

Test coverage:
I verified the added test suite locally with `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest optional-skills/github-ci-watch/tests -q` (3 passed). GitHub CI is still pending on the main repo matrix as of review time.

No blocking issues from my read.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: feat(agent): emit a turn_failed event on any turn failure (chainlink #299)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Summary
This change closes the visibility half of chainlink #299 by emitting a `turn_failed` event for any turn that exits through the common error path. The placement is right: it covers all trigger types without disturbing the existing `turn_timeout` and `quota_exhausted` specialty events, and the regression test exercises the silent-failure shape that motivated the PR.

## Observations
No blocking issues. The implementation is small, correctly targeted, and the test checks the load-bearing fields (`trigger`, `channel_id`, and error text).

## Test coverage
The added regression test is appropriate for the bug: it forces an agent failure on a poller-triggered turn and asserts the event lands in `events.jsonl` exactly once.

## Non-blocking
The PR body clearly scopes this as the visibility half only; that's useful because the retry half lives in the poller skill rather than in mimir core.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: refactor(quota): per-provider quota-window registry; wire Minimax + Codex into the agent usage view (chainlink #298)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Summary
This refactor fixes the agent-facing quota view gap for non-Anthropic providers by moving quota-window definitions into a single per-provider registry and deriving both the billing-provider window maps and the resource-usage rendering maps from it. The shape is clean: `quota_windows.py` is pure data, the dependency graph stays acyclic, and the new tests protect both directions of drift.

## Observations
- `mimir/quota_windows.py` is the right cut point. It owns the provider prefix, display label, and projection window length in one place, which is exactly the data that had been split across `billing.py` and `rate_limits.py`.
- Wiring `rate_limits._LABEL` and `_WINDOW_HOURS` from the registry closes the actual user-visible bug: Minimax / Codex keys now render with proper labels and participate in off-pace projection.
- The anti-drift tests are the important part here, not just the refactor itself. `tests/test_quota_windows.py` and the added `test_rate_limits.py` cases make it much less likely this regresses the next time a provider is added.

## Testing
I spot-ran `uv run pytest -q tests/test_quota_windows.py tests/test_rate_limits.py -q` locally in the PR worktree; it passed. GitHub CI is green as well.

Verdict: APPROVE.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: fix(setup): report the effective runtime MIMIR_MODEL_SPEC, not the --model/default route (chainlink #297)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
Summary:
This fixes two real mismatches in setup/model routing: the setup banner now reports the effective runtime model spec when `MIMIR_MODEL_SPEC` is present in the process environment, and `detect_route()` now correctly treats explicit `codex-plus:*` specs as OpenAI subscription routes instead of falling through to the anthropic/API default. The implementation matches the runtime behavior described in the PR, and the added tests cover both regressions directly.

Observations:
- `setup_home()` still scaffolds `<home>/.env` from the `--model`/default route, but the reported status fields now switch to the env-resolved route when that's what `mimir run` will actually use. The extra banner note makes the distinction explicit instead of silently contradicting runtime behavior.
- The new `codex-plus:` branch in `detect_route()` is the right place for the fix. It mirrors the existing `claude-code:` explicit-spec handling and ensures provider/billing/monitor metadata stay coherent for pre-qualified subscription specs.
- Test coverage is good for the scope here: `tests/test_cli.py` covers the setup-banner env override path and fallback behavior, and `tests/test_model_registry.py` covers both explicit `codex-plus:*` routing and the invariant that the explicit spec stays subscription-mode regardless of the `--subscription` flag.

I didn't find any blocking issues in the diff.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: feat(saga): add codex_plus LLM provider — ride the ChatGPT/Codex subscription (chainlink #296)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Review: feat(saga): add codex_plus LLM provider

**Verdict: Approve.** Clean, well-structured addition that fits naturally into the existing provider dispatch pattern. The rationale (subscription-sharing, no API credit, native async) is sound and the live end-to-end verification against `gpt-5.4-mini` is reassuring. A few observations below — none block landing.

---

### What the PR does

Adds a fourth provider path to `mimir/saga/_llm.py::call_llm`. The new `codex_plus` branch routes saga's internal LLM calls (triple extraction, consolidation, rerank, etc.) through `langchain_codex_plus.ChatCodexPlus` — authenticated against `~/.codex` OAuth, no API key needed. Comes with hermetic tests, a `_flatten_text` helper, and updated observability-regression tests.

---

### Correctness

- **Dispatch ordering** — `codex_plus` branch inserted before `anthropic`, consistent with the `claude_code` branch above it. No case falls through incorrectly.
- **`_flatten_text` placement** — defined after `call_llm` but before `_call_codex_plus_async`, which is the only caller. Python resolves names at call time, so this works, but it reads slightly back-to-front. Minor.
- **`ImportError` test simulation** — `monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "langchain_codex_plus", None)` correctly triggers `ModuleNotFoundError` (an `ImportError` subclass) on the lazy `from langchain_codex_plus import ...` inside the function. Pattern mirrors how the `anthropic` path's test fakes are structured.
- **Lazy imports** — consistent with the `anthropic` path (`from anthropic import Anthropic` inside the sync function). Correct approach for an optional extra.

---

### Observations

**1. `call_llm` function-level docstring not updated**

The module-level docstring (lines 15-19 in the diff) correctly lists all four providers. But `call_llm`'s own docstring still says:

```
Provider dispatch:
- ``claude_code`` runs on the caller's event loop via ...
- ``anthropic`` and ``openai_compat`` are sync HTTP libraries ...
```

`codex_plus` isn't mentioned. Minor gap — a reader looking only at the function signature will miss it.

**2. `max_tokens` / `temperature` silently ignored**

Documented in the docstring ("accepted but unused") and PR body, so not hidden. But saga callers set `max_tokens` for a reason (e.g., bounded extraction output). If Codex ever surfaces these params through `ChatCodexPlus`, the silent drop will need a revisit. Consider adding a one-line `# TODO: wire when ChatCodexPlus exposes max_tokens/temperature` comment at the construction site so it doesn't get forgotten in a future Codex API update.

**3. Per-call `ChatCodexPlus` construction**

The justification (different event loops across cron vs chat) is valid. Construction cost is low (pydantic init + local file read). At saga's ~9 calls per consolidation cycle, this creates 9 HTTP client instances per cycle — each authenticated against the same `~/.codex` file. Should be fine in practice. If auth-file reads ever show up in profiling, a per-loop client cache keyed on `id(asyncio.get_running_loop())` would be the fix, but that's premature for now.

**4. Rate-limit callback gap (tracked)**

`_call_codex_plus_async` doesn't wire a `rate_limit_callback` the way the `anthropic` path does. The PR body explicitly tracks this as a follow-up — and there's even a `NOTE:` comment in the docstring. No action needed here, just confirming the deferral is visible.

---

### Test coverage

Solid. The new test file covers all the branches I'd want:
- `_flatten_text` with str / list-of-str / list-of-dict / list-of-obj / None inputs
- Successful dispatch with model + `reasoning_effort` verification
- Default model when not specified
- List content flattening end-to-end
- Runtime failure → empty string + warning log
- Missing `codex-plus` extra → empty string + warning log
- `call_llm` dispatch routing

The existing no-warning test being updated to add `codex_plus` as a recognized provider is the right hygiene.

---

### M

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: fix(update): --no-cache-dir on the pending-update pip install (chainlink #295)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
**Verdict: Approve** — clean fix, correct diagnosis, minimal blast radius.

## What this does

Adds `--no-cache-dir` to the pip argv in `_run_pip_install` so self-updates always re-fetch the package index. Directly addresses the "No matching distribution found" failure mode that bit muninn 0.2.1 and 0.2.3: pip's stale cached simple-index returns a version list that pre-dates the just-published release, the flag is consumed on failure, and the agent silently stays pinned.

## Observations

- **Correct fix for the failure mode.** `--no-cache-dir` is the canonical pip solution for post-release index lag. Alternative approaches (`pip cache purge` before install) would have wider side effects; this is appropriately scoped.
- **One call site.** `_run_pip_install` is called exactly once in `apply_pending_update` — no risk of unintended effect elsewhere.
- **Test coverage is adequate.** The new assertion (`"--no-cache-dir" in argv`) in `test_apply_happy_path_runs_pip_then_execs` pins the flag in the happy-path argv. Full suite passes (3946 passed, 5 skipped).
- **Docstring updated** to match the new argv. Comment in the code block is verbose (~7 lines for a one-word addition) but clear; no correctness concern, minor style note.
- **Minor downside acknowledged.** Self-updates now bypass the cache, so every update re-downloads from the index. Cost is negligible for an infrequent operation; the silent-stay-pinned failure is far worse.

No issues that warrant blocking.

payload.body:
## Review: chore(release): 0.2.3

**Verdict: Approve ✅**

Standard release PR — minimal, mechanical, correct.

### What changed
Three files touched:
- `pyproject.toml` — `version` bumped 0.2.2 → 0.2.3 ✓
- `mimir/__init__.py` — `__version__` bumped 0.2.2 → 0.2.3 ✓
- `CHANGELOG.md` — new `[0.2.3]` section + updated footer links ✓

### Checks
- **Version consistency**: all three version strings agree on 0.2.3.
- **CHANGELOG section**: covers all 7 PRs (#499, #500, #501, #503, #504, #505, #506) with chainlink refs, correct Added/Changed/Fixed structure, and today's date (2026-05-31).

## Review: feat(scaffold-docker): install codex CLI for codex-subscription agents

**Verdict: Approve.** Clean, minimal, well-tested. The provider-conditional approach is the right call.

---

### What this does

Adds `__CODEX_INSTALL__` placeholder to both Dockerfile templates (workspace + pypi), substituted to `RUN npm install -g @openai/codex` when `codex-plus` is among the deployment's extras — otherwise a no-op comment. The extras detection correctly branches on `mimir_extras` (pypi) vs `uv_extras` (workspace).

### Strengths

- **Provider-conditional, not unconditional.** Non-codex images stay untouched. Right call — this is a model-provider dependency, not a skill fragment, and the PR correctly justifies avoiding the `dockerfile.fragment` mechanism for that reason.
- **No stray sentinel.** `test_render_dockerfile_omits_codex_by_default` asserts `__CODEX_INSTALL__` is always substituted. Good sentinel hygiene.
- **Consistent pattern.** `__CODEX_INSTALL__` / `_codex_install_block()` mirrors the existing `__USERDEL_BLOCK__` / `_USERDEL_BLOCK` pattern exactly — same `base.replace()` shape, same helper-function separation.
- **Dependency satisfied.** #505 (`spawn_codex`) merged ~6 min ago, so the binary this installs is actually callable.

### Minor observations (non-blocking)

1. **No version pin.** `npm install -g @openai/codex` floats at latest. This is consistent with the existing `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` pattern (also unpinned), so not a new issue — but worth noting both are supply-chain risk surface. A `@openai/codex@0.135.0` pin (the version the PR was verified against) would make the image reproducible.

2. **No-op comment always present.** Every non-codex Dockerfile will contain `# (codex CLI not installed — no codex-plus extra selected)`. It's not wrong, but it reads slightly odd in a Dockerfile that has nothing to do with codex. Omitting the placeholder entirely (returning `""` when `install_codex=False`) plus stripping the surrounding blank lines would be cleaner — though that's more fiddly template surgery than it's worth for a comment.

3. **Workspace negative case missing.** `test_scaffold_installs_codex_for_workspace_uv_extra` only asserts the positive case. The pypi test covers both positive and negative within one test function; workspace has no negative assertion. Low risk (the `render_dockerfile` unit tests cover the general gate), but a symmetry gap.

### Tests

Full suite (3946 passed, 5 skipped) confirmed in the PR. Four new tests cover the gate for both modes × both directions (except workspace negative, noted above). Good coverage for the scope of the change.

LGTM.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Review: spawn_codex — one-shot Codex exec (chainlink #293)

Good implementation. The `spawn_claude_code` mirror is faithful and the shared `_SpawnGuard` reuse is exactly the right call — one budget across both spawn paths is architecturally clean and prevents the fork-bomb via either vector.

### Correctness ✓

Rate-slot accounting is correct throughout:
- Depth check fires before `_spawn_acquire_rate_slot`, so no slot is reserved on depth-cap return (no release needed).
- `_spawn_acquire_rate_slot` only appends to `guard.recent` on success, so the `rate_err is not None` early-return path is clean.
- The `BaseException` handler correctly releases the rate slot on abnormal exit before the semaphore is held, matching `spawn_claude_code`'s shape.
- Timeout and `FileNotFoundError` paths consume the slot (intentional — matches sibling behavior).

### Issues

**`import shlex` inside the function body** — minor but worth fixing. `shlex` is stdlib, should be at the module top with the other imports, not inline after `cwd_path = ...`. No runtime impact but breaks the convention held everywhere else in `registry.py`.

**Rate-error message replacement is fragile:**
```python
return rate_err.replace("spawn_claude_code", "spawn_codex")
```
This works today but will silently mismatch if `_spawn_acquire_rate_slot`'s error string ever changes. The clean fix (not required here) would be parameterizing the tool name in `_spawn_acquire_rate_slot`. Worth a chainlink follow-up if not addressed now.

**`MIMIR_CODEX_SPAWN_ARGS` + `model` flag ordering** — if the env var contains `--model foo` AND the caller passes `model=bar`, codex gets duplicate `--model` flags. Most CLIs take last-wins, but worth a one-line doc note in the docstring.

### Test coverage gap

`spawn_codex` tests cover coroutine wiring, missing config, and argv construction — but `spawn_claude_code` has four additional tests this PR doesn't mirror:
- Empty/whitespace prompt rejection
- `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` path
- `FileNotFoundError` (missing CLI)
- Model flag omission (no `--model` when not passed)

These aren't blocking but the parity would be good to have. The timeout and FileNotFoundError paths are especially worth covering since the behavior (rate slot consumed, specific error string) is non-obvious.

### The "best-effort invocation" note

The PR body is appropriately honest about `codex exec` flags being unverified. The `MIMIR_CODEX_SPAWN_ARGS` escape hatch is the right design — keeps the core code stable while letting the operator tune to the actual CLI version. ✓

### Summary

Approvable. The one mechanical fix I'd want before merge is the `import shlex` placement. The error-replacement fragility and test parity gaps are worth follow-up chainlinks but don't block.

## Review: feat(providers): gate spawn_claude_code on claude-code availability (PR3/3, chainlink #292)

**Verdict: Approve** — clean, well-scoped, correct. One minor observation below.

---

### What this does

Moves `spawn_claude_code` out of the static `tools = [...]` list and into a conditional `append` gated on `claude_code_available()` (a `shutil.which("claude")` check). Adds a `requires_cli` field to `ProviderSpec` to carry the dependency declaratively, and wires it to `_ANTHROPIC_MAX`. Mirrors the existing `web_tools_enabled()` pattern exactly — the placement in `all_mimir_tools()` is consistent.

---

### Code quality

**Correct.** The core logic is a one-liner — `shutil.which(cli) is not None` — no state, no side effects, trivially testable. The `requires_cli` field has a sensible default (`""` = no CLI dependency) and is forward-compatible if other providers grow similar needs.

**Tests.** Monkeypatching `P.shutil.which` is the right surface — the module imports `shutil` (not `from shutil import which`), so the patch sticks. The two-state test (path present / path absent) is sufficient for this function.

---

### One observation: the `or "claude"` fallback

```python
cli = _ANTHROPIC_MAX.requires_cli or "claude"
```

`_ANTHROPIC_MAX.requires_cli` is `"claude"`, so the `or` branch is never taken in practice. The defensive fallback is harmless but slightly misleading — it implies the field could be empty, in which case the function still checks for `"claude"` rather than returning `True` (no CLI required) or `False`. If the intent is "if the spec has no CLI dependency, we still check for claude because this function is specifically about claude-code availability", that's fine — but it's worth a one-line comment or simplifying to:

```python
return shutil.which(_ANTHROPIC_MAX.requires_cli or "claude") is not None
```

(same thing, just inline). Minor nit — not a blocker.

---

### Deferred items (well-reasoned)

- **Embedding-provider selection** — correct call: embedding vendors and LLM providers are independent taxonomies; folding them into `ProviderSpec` would be a category error.
- **Credential-based discovery** — correct call: compat gateways share the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` envelope, so `active_providers` over-reports without a `cred_verify` model first.
- **Auth-state probing** — correct call: present-but-unauthed surfaces the tool, fails at call time. Heavier introspection deferred appropriately.

---

3937 passed, 3 files changed (+52/-2), stacked correctly on slice2. Good to go once #501→#502 land.

payload.body:
## Verdict: Approve

### Summary

Clean final slice. The gating logic is correct: `spawn_claude_code` moves out of the static `all_mimir_tools()` list and into a conditional `append` behind `claude_code_available()`, which delegates to `shutil.which` against `_ANTHROPIC_MAX.requires_cli`. The `requires_cli` field is a well-chosen point of extensibility on `ProviderSpec` for future CLI-dependent tools or providers; the fallback `or "claude"` in `claude_code_available` is a reasonable belt-and-suspenders guard against an accidental empty-string in `requires_cli`, though in practice the frozen dataclass default `""` would never be used for `_ANTHROPIC_MAX` once `requires_cli="claude"` is set.

### Gating logic — correct and safe

`mimir/providers.py` — `claude_code_available()` is a pure `shutil.which` check, no side effects, cheap to call at registration time. Gating on presence rather than auth state is the explicitly stated and correct tradeoff: auth probing would require a subprocess call on every startup and the failure mode (tool registered but unauthenticated → call-time error) is no worse than before this PR and is identical to the existing web-tools gate's behavior. The `_ANTHROPIC_MAX.requires_cli or "claude"` fallback is redundant but harmless.

`mimir/tools/registry.py` — the placement of the `spawn_claude_code` gate after web tools and before MCP tools is sensible and consistent with the surrounding `web_tools_enabled()` pattern. The deferred import (`from ..providers import claude_code_available`) mirrors the style of the `from .mcp import get_mcp_tools` import a few lines later; a top-level import would be equally fine, but there's no correctness issue either way.

### Test coverage

`tests/test_providers.py` — the `test_claude_code_available_reflects_cli_on_path` test covers both the true and false branches via `monkeypatch` on `shutil.which` (correctly patching the module attribute `P.shutil` rather than the function in the `shutil` module namespace). 

One gap worth noting: there is no test that asserts `spawn_claude_code` is absent from `all_mimir_tools()` when the CLI is missing, or present when it is. The existing `test_tool_wiring.py` exercises the function itself (async wiring, argument routing, timeout handling) but not list membership. This is a non-blocking omission — the PR description explicitly acknowledges "Tool-wiring tests untouched (they exercise the function, not list membership)" — and the function-level tests are thorough. A membership test would close the loop but is not required for correctness.

### Minor / non-blocking observations

1. **`requires_cli` docstring placement** (`mimir/providers.py` L105–112): the new `Runtime:` section in the class docstring sits inside the `Quota:` section's text block visually (no blank line separates the end of the quota description from `Runtime:`). The actual rendered doc reads correctly because it's a new header, but adding a blank line before `Runtime:` would improve visual separation in raw source.

2. **`_ANTHROPIC_MAX` is not exported in `__all__`** (if one exists) — but `providers.py` has no `__all__`, so this is not an issue. The `PROVIDERS` tuple (which includes `_ANTHROPIC_MAX`) is public and already tested.

3. The PR description's deferred-items section is well-written and accurately captures why embedding-provider selection and credential-based discovery are out of scope here.

Overall: the change is small, targeted, well-tested, and fails gracefully (CLI absent → tool not registered; CLI present but unauthed → tool registered, fails at call time with a clear error). Ready to merge once #501 and #502 land.

## PR #502 — registry-driven adapter extras + setup hint

**Verdict: Approve.** Small, targeted, fixes a real bug. Tested off the slice2 branch: `test_providers` (including new `test_extra_for_spec`) + `test_agent` pass clean.

---

### What this does
- Adds `SPEC_PREFIX_EXTRAS` dict + `extra_for_spec()` to providers.py — the per-spec-prefix pip extra map.
- **Bug fix:** `agent._build_chat_model`'s ImportError hint said `pip install 'mimir[codex-plus]'` (wrong distribution name). Now sources the extra from the registry and corrects to `mimir-agent[{extra}]`.
- **Setup hint:** `mimir setup` now prints `model adapter: pip install mimir-agent[<extra>]` for the chosen model spec, so operators install the langchain adapter at setup time rather than discovering it via a runtime ImportError.

---

### Observations

**Dict-vs-ProviderSpec for extras:**
`SPEC_PREFIX_EXTRAS` is keyed by spec prefix (not by provider), which is the right granularity — Minimax and direct Anthropic both use the `anthropic:` prefix and both need `langchain-anthropic`, so the map correctly returns `"anthropic"` for both. The alternative (adding an `extra` field to `ProviderSpec`) would need extra fields to handle multi-prefix-same-extra vs same-prefix-different-extra. The current dict is cleaner for this axis.

**`claude-code` intentionally absent:**
Comment + test both document this. ✓

**Inside-function import in setup.py:**
`from ..providers import extra_for_spec` inside `_print_setup_report` is consistent with how other imports in that file are structured (billing.build_quota_providers, etc.) — fine.

**`extra_for_spec` on a bare name:**
`extra_for_spec("claude-sonnet-4-6")` → prefix `""` → returns `""` → no hint printed. ✓ Operators using bare names haven't resolved their spec yet (setup hasn't been called?), so silence is correct.

**`extra_for_spec` on unknown prefix:**
Falls to `SPEC_PREFIX_EXTRAS.get(prefix, "")` → `""`. Safe default.

Nothing blocking.

payload.body:
## Verdict: Approve

PR2 of the provider registry chainlink does exactly what it says: centralizes adapter-extra names in `providers.SPEC_PREFIX_EXTRAS` / `extra_for_spec()`, wires the two consumers, and fixes the `mimir` → `mimir-agent` bug in the `codex-plus` ImportError hint. Code is clean and the new `test_extra_for_spec` parametrize block covers all the meaningful cases (known prefixes, `claude-code` special case, bare name, empty string).

### Specific observations

**`mimir/providers.py` (new additions)**

- `SPEC_PREFIX_EXTRAS` and `extra_for_spec` are clean. The fallback `""` and the `.lower()` normalization are correct; the `partition(":")` avoids the off-by-one that `split(":", 1)[0]` would have for a bare name like `"anthropic"` — wait, actually both behave identically there, but `partition` is the right idiom. No issues.
- The docstring clearly explains the `claude-code` intentional absence. Good.

**`mimir/agent.py`**

- The `extra_for_spec(spec) or "codex-plus"` fallback is a safe guard but will never actually fire (the spec prefix at that branch is always `"codex-plus"`) — it's harmless belt-and-suspenders.
- **Non-blocking: dead code.** `_PROVIDER_EXTRAS` (defined at line 206 in `agent.py`, introduced in PR1) is never referenced anywhere in the file. - **Minor: missing shell quoting.** Line 1561 prints `pip install mimir-agent[{adapter_extra}]` without quoting the brackets. In `zsh` (and some `bash` configurations with `failglob`/`nullglob`) unquoted `[...]` is treated as a glob pattern and will error or expand unexpectedly. The `agent.py` change correctly quotes it as `'mimir-agent[{extra}]'`. Suggest making the setup hint consistent: `pip install 'mimir-agent[{adapter_extra}]'`.

**`tests/test_providers.py`**

- Parametrize covers all branches. The `"anthropic:MiniMax-M2.7"` case is a nice nod to the compat-gateway note. No gaps.

Solid PR. Two non-blocking findings: remove the duplicate dead `_PROVIDER_EXTRAS` dict in `agent.py`, and add shell quoting around the setup hint's install command. Neither blocks merge — the functionality is correct and the bug fix (wrong package name in the ImportError hint) is valuable.

## PR #501 — unified provider registry (routing + quota)

**Verdict: Approve.** Clean DRY refactor. The parity suite caught the one behaviour-preserving subtlety (MiniMax case-sensitivity) and the tests pin it explicitly. A few things worth noting below, none blocking.

---

### What this does
Single `ProviderSpec` per provider with two resolvers:
- `provider_for_model_name` (forward: bare name → provider, used by `detect_route`)
- `provider_for_quota` (reverse: spec + base URL → provider, used by `build_quota_providers`)

All existing PROVIDER_* constants re-exported from model_registry for back-compat. Confirmed: `test_model_registry` (26) + `test_billing` (58) + new `test_providers` pass cleanly off the branch.

---

### Observations

**Dead field on `_ANTHROPIC_MAX`:**
`_ANTHROPIC_MAX.subscription_monitor_label` is set to the Anthropic OAuth label, but it can never be read. `detect_route` only uses `prov.subscription_monitor_label` in the `subscription and prov.subscription_spec_prefix` branch — and `_ANTHROPIC_MAX.subscription_spec_prefix` is `""`. Since `_ANTHROPIC_MAX` also has no `name_prefixes`, `provider_for_model_name` never returns it, so the subscription branch is unreachable for that spec. The field is dead code. The functional label lives on `_ANTHROPIC_API` where it belongs. Cosmetic, but worth removing to avoid "why is this here?" confusion on the next read.

**Duplicate label string:**
The `"Anthropic OAuth quota poller (5h + 7d windows)"` string appears on both `_ANTHROPIC_MAX` and `_ANTHROPIC_API`. Given the above, the one on `_ANTHROPIC_MAX` is dead, but if it were live the two could drift. A module-level `_ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_MONITOR_LABEL` constant would make this a one-edit update.

**`_default_provider()` guard:**
Good call making it a `RuntimeError` instead of returning `None`. The guard is cheap insurance against a future table edit that removes `is_default`.

**`provider_for_quota` precedence:**
The `prefix != "anthropic"` guard in the inner loop is the right mechanical expression of "anthropic: is ambiguous, fall to host matching." The comment in the docstring explains it clearly. ✓

**`test_quota_keys_are_all_buildable`:**
This cross-module table-invariant test is the best one in the file — it'll catch a typo'd `quota_provider_key` the moment it's added. Keep the pattern for PR3's `cred_env_keys`.

## Approved — clean refactor, all parity nets green

This PR delivers slice 1 of the unified provider registry (chainlink #292) exactly as described. The separation of concerns is correct: `providers.py` holds the taxonomy once; `detect_route` and `build_quota_providers` become thin consumers. All 132 relevant tests pass (26 routing + 58 billing parity nets + 33 new registry surface tests, plus full suite 3929 passed).

### Specific observations

**`mimir/providers.py`**

- `field` is imported from `dataclasses` but never used (line 35). Minor, but worth cleaning up.
- `_ANTHROPIC_MAX` has a `subscription_monitor_label` set to the OAuth label string inline (line 166 in the local file) rather than referencing `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_MONITOR_LABEL`. The PR's version (head ref) omits it entirely since `_ANTHROPIC_MAX` is never the result of a forward lookup — the label there is unreachable, and the comment explains this. The local working tree has diverged slightly, but the PR head is clean.
- `provider_for_model_name` checks `name_prefixes_exact` and then `name_prefixes` within the same provider iteration. This is safe with the current table (MiniMax owns both its exact and insensitive prefixes on the same `ProviderSpec`), but worth documenting that exact-before-insensitive is per-provider, not a global priority — a future table edit adding an exact match on a later provider could be surprised by an earlier provider's insensitive match winning.
- The `_default_provider()` guard (`raise RuntimeError`) is the right defense for a future table edit that accidentally removes `is_default`.

- One gap: no test for Moonshot + `--subscription` through `detect_route` (verifies it stays on `anthropic:` spec rather than flipping wire protocol, since `subscription_spec_prefix=""` for Moonshot). The billing parity net covers the quota side; the routing side is covered in `test_model_registry`, so this is acceptable for this slice.

- Remove the unused `field` import in `providers.py`.
- Update the `detect_route` module-level docstring "Add a new provider" instructions to point to `providers.py` instead.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
## Review: chainlink #286 — UpdateDigest + helpers

**Verdict: Request changes** — one functional bug that nullifies the headline surface, plus a test that hides it.

### 🔴 Blocking — `_scheduler_delta` reads the wrong schema, so it always returns `[]`

`_tick_names` does:

```python
data = yaml.safe_load(raw) or {}
jobs = data.get("jobs") or {}
if isinstance(jobs, dict):
    return set(jobs.keys())
```

But `scheduler.yaml` / `scheduler_template.yaml` are **top-level YAML lists**, not a `{jobs: {...}}` mapping. The bundled template:

```yaml
- name: heartbeat
  cron: "0 * * * *"
  prompt_file: heartbeat.md
- name: reflect
  ...
```

So `yaml.safe_load` returns a `list`; `list.get("jobs")` raises `AttributeError`; the bare `except` swallows it; `_tick_names` returns `set()` for **both** files. `template_names - live_names` is therefore always empty → `_scheduler_delta` always returns `[]` on real data. The scheduler-delta surface is the primary ask of chainlink #284 ("prompt them to add scheduled tasks"), so this is the one that most needs to work.

Confirmed: the bundled template has 4 top-level `- name:` entries and 0 `jobs:` keys, and `scheduler.load_jobs()` parses it as a list.

Fix — parse the list shape:

```python
def _tick_names(path: Path) -> set[str]:
    try:
        data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or []
        if isinstance(data, list):
            return {e["name"] for e in data if isinstance(e, dict) and "name" in e}
    except Exception:
        pass
    return set()
```

### 🔴 Blocking — the tests encode the wrong schema, so they pass green while the feature is dead

`test_scheduler_delta_returns_missing_ticks` and `test_scheduler_delta_no_delta_when_live_has_all` build fixtures as `yaml.dump({"jobs": {"heartbeat": {}, ...}})` — the same `{jobs: {...}}` shape the buggy impl assumes. They validate a contract the real files don't use, which is exactly why the bug shipped green. Please rebuild the fixtures in the real list form (`[{"name": "heartbeat", ...}, ...]`); a fixture that loads / asserts against the actual `mimir/scheduler_template.yaml` would be even stronger.

### 🟠 Secondary — `_env_gaps` reads stale builtin-skills at compute time

`_compute_update_digest` runs inside `apply_pending_update` **pre-`execv`**, but `_env_gaps` reads `<home>/.mimir_builtin_skills/*/SKILL.md`, which is only re-seeded from the new package **after** `execv` (during the new code's boot). So at compute time it reflects the *old* version's skill requirements — a newly-added skill's required env var won't be surfaced. The `_env_gaps` docstring claims the opposite ("refreshed before `consume_update_digest` runs"). `_scheduler_delta` avoids this by reading the bundled template straight from the installed (new) package; `_env_gaps` should do the same (read the new package's skill defs directly), or the diff computation should move to consume-time while still capturing `prior_version` pre-`execv`.

### 👍 Looks good

`UpdateDigest` + `to_dict`/`from_dict` roundtrip, the `_current_version()` importlib.metadata fallback, and the `detect_skill_drift` wiring are clean. Once the scheduler schema + tests are fixed (and ideally the env_gaps timing), happy to re-review.

payload.title: fix(packaging): bundle runtime data files in wheel + release 0.2.2 (chainlink #290)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Review: fix(packaging): bundle runtime data files in wheel + release 0.2.2

**Verdict: Approve ✅**

### What this does

Fixes a silent packaging bug present since 0.2.0 where several files the installed package reads at runtime were missing from the published wheel. The `[tool.hatch.build].include` allowlist either had dead globs (pointing at `mimir/prompts/` instead of `mimir/prompt_templates/`) or extension-specific patterns that silently dropped new support-file types (`.sh`, `.fragment`). The only deployments not bitten were existing installs with persistent saga DBs and already-seeded homes.

### Code quality

**`pyproject.toml` changes — solid.**

- Each include entry now has a comment explaining *which runtime path reads it and why* — good, because this list will be consulted years from now by someone wondering if they can remove an entry.
- `mimir/skills/**/*` (whole subtree) over the old extension-specific allowlist is the right choice: support-file types won't silently regress when a skill adds a new extension. The "but what about `.pyc`" concern is addressed correctly by the parenthetical — hatchling intersects with VCS-tracked files, so gitignored artifacts stay out.
- `mimir/saga/*.sql` is the right scope — SQL files directly in `mimir/saga/`. If migrations ever live in a subdirectory, a new glob will be needed; that's a future-problem and the regression test will catch it.

**`tests/test_wheel_package_data.py` — well-crafted.**

- Stdlib-only (`tomllib` + `re`): runs anywhere pytest runs, no build-time dependency on `uv`/`hatchling`/`pathspec`. Good tradeoff.
- `_gitwildmatch_to_regex` covers exactly the three constructs the include list uses (`**/`, `*`, `?`). `test_gitwildmatch_to_regex_semantics` pins the key behaviors explicitly — this is the right way to guard a hand-rolled regex translator.
- `CRITICAL_RUNTIME_DATA` serves as living documentation of the package's runtime dependency surface. The comment "keeping this list current is the whole point of the guard" is the right reminder.
- The test reads from the *actual* `pyproject.toml`, so it will catch future regressions if someone edits the include list without updating the manifest.

**One minor divergence risk (non-blocking):** `_gitwildmatch_to_regex` is an approximation of `pathspec` (hatchling's actual glob engine). For the patterns currently in use it's faithful; if a future pattern uses `[!...]` character classes or `{a,b}` brace expansion, the test's regex won't handle it and will either false-positive or false-negative silently. This is fine today and the `test_gitwildmatch_to_regex_semantics` test makes any future divergence discoverable.

**`optional-skills` coverage confirmed:** I verified `mimir/skills/optional-skills/` is nested inside `mimir/skills/`, so `mimir/skills/**/*` already covers it — no separate entry needed.

### CHANGELOG / version bump

Clean: both `__init__.py` and `pyproject.toml` bumped to 0.2.2, the `[Unreleased]` comparison link updated to `v0.2.2...HEAD`, and the new `[0.2.2]` tag link added. CHANGELOG entry is accurate and thorough.

### Verification

PR description states `uv build` confirmed all 10 critical files present in rebuilt wheel, zero `.pyc`/`__pycache__` entries, and 3888 passed / 5 skipped locally. The regression test provides a repeatable guard so the "did I forget to update the include list?" question is now machine-answerable.

Nothing blocking here.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Verdict: APPROVE

Clean, well-scoped dead-code removal. The approach is sound, the PR description is thorough, and 3893 tests pass.

## Summary

Removes `NvidiaNimProvider` (never instantiated in practice — every live agent uses voyage), makes `voyage` the code-level default everywhere NIM was hardcoded, and removes the `nvidia-nim` setup preset. The local bge/onnx fallback and the `[llm]` chat subsystem default are correctly preserved and explicitly called out as out of scope.

## Observations

**`_config_io.py` — latent bug fixed (good catch)**
The old `_DEFAULTS["embedding"]` had `api_key_env = "OPENAI_API_KEY"` even though the provider was `nvidia-nim` — wrong key. This was never exercised because NIM was never actually used, but it would have silently misfired the auto-fallback check for any agent that did configure NIM. Fixed to `VOYAGE_API_KEY` for voyage. Worth the explicit call-out: this is a correctness fix, not just a rename.

**`VoyageProvider.was_set_in_toml` override — may now be simplifiable (non-blocking)**
Now that `_DEFAULTS["embedding"]["url"]` is the voyage URL, `_cfg('embedding', 'url', ...)` in `OpenAIProvider.__init__()` should already return the voyage URL for a minimal saga.toml. The `was_set_in_toml` guard in `VoyageProvider.__init__` might be redundant (the base class gets the right URL from `_DEFAULTS` rather than an OpenAI-shaped hardcoded fallback). Harmless either way and the comment explains the history; flagging as a potential simplification for a follow-up, not a blocker.

**Pre-existing: `_PROVIDER_AUTO_THRESHOLDS["voyage"]` is `0.80` but docs say `0.92` (not introduced here)**
`setup.py` help text and the inline `_default_saga_toml` comment both say `0.92 for voyage/fastembed`, but the actual dict in `embeddings.py` has `"voyage": 0.80`. This PR only removes the `nvidia-nim` row and doesn't change the voyage value, so not a regression — but the doc/code mismatch is real. Probably worth a separate cleanup PR.

**Test removal is correct** — `test_setup_embedding_nvidia_nim_preset` tests behavior that no longer exists; dropping it is the right call.

payload.title: scheduler: issues-audit (monthly) + commitments-review (weekly) backlog ticks (#164, #283)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Overview

Clean implementation of the two validity-sweep scheduled ticks (#164 issues-audit, #283 commitments-review). Well-modeled on `reflect.md` — the autonomy boundaries baked into both prompts are calibrated well (retire autonomous only on confirmed RESOLVED, dismiss escalate-by-default). Deploy note in the PR description is clear about the seed_scheduler no-op for existing homes.

## Code quality and conventions

**Prompt templates**

- Both follow the reflect.md frontmatter shape faithfully (name/description/allowed-tools + human-readable body). Tests verify this structurally.
- Autonomy decision trees (keep / verb-with-teeth / raise-as-chainlink-bug / escalate) are the right shape. The self-reminders section at the end of each template is load-bearing — good that it's there.
- `commitments-review`: `mark COMPLETED needs hard evidence` and `DISMISS is escalate-by-default` are exactly right given what the commitments store is for.
- `issues-audit`: cursor-resume pattern across monthly runs is a good budget-discipline design; wrapping to the top when exhausted is explicit.

**scheduler_template.yaml**

Crons look correct:
- `0 7 1 * *` → 1st of month, 07:00 UTC ✓
- `0 7 * * 1` → Mondays, 07:00 UTC ✓

Comment block updated accurately from "Two" to "Four" recurring ticks ✓

**Tests**

Both tests are well-targeted: wiring (template exists, cron parses, prompt_file resolves) and structure (frontmatter fields + chainlink ref present). No behavioral tests needed for natural-language prompt bodies.

## Findings

**Minor — `allowed-tools` frontmatter is incomplete (documentation gap, not functional)**

`issues-audit.md` uses `rebuild_index` (Step 3) and `send_message` (Step 4); neither is listed in the frontmatter. `commitments-review.md` uses `send_message` (Step 3); also absent. However: `reflect.md` has the same pattern — it uses `send_message` in its body without listing it in `allowed-tools`. So this is advisory/doc convention, not a runtime-enforced constraint. Low urgency, but worth a follow-up to bring consistency across all three templates.

**Minor — cursor file path is borderline against filing rules**

Step 1 writes the cursor to `state/issues-audit-cursor.md` — top-level `state/`. The filing rules call this a drift-amplifier misfile: "nothing lives at top-level state/ except auto-meta, operator-managed yaml, or named singletons with explicit purpose (heartbeat-backlog.md, proposed-changes.md)." A cursor is arguably a named singleton with explicit purpose, so this is a judgment call. But a path like `state/audit/issues-audit-cursor.md` or `state/reports/` would be tidier and unambiguously inside the rules. Not blocking.

**Nice-to-have — commitments-review Step 1 hedge**

"Use whatever status/open filter `mimir commitments list --help` exposes" is softer than the rest of the prompt's tone. The commitments CLI is already in-tree; could be a concrete flag reference rather than a help-page punt.

## Summary

Both prompts do what they say, the tests cover the wiring, and the autonomy calibration is solid. The two minor findings are documentation-quality, not correctness. **Approve.**

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: fix(index): unique per-call tmp names + orphan sweep (chainlink #272)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
The unique-per-call tmp name is a correct, real improvement and the happy-path tests are solid. Two things to address before merge.

### 1. (blocking) The orphan sweep can delete a *live, in-flight* tmp from a concurrent process — re-opening the FileNotFoundError this PR fixes
`_sweep_orphaned_tmps` globs `<index>.tmp.*` and unlinks every match, with no way to tell an orphan from a tmp another process is mid-write on:
```python
for orphan in path.parent.glob(path.name + ".tmp.*"):
    orphan.unlink(missing_ok=True)
```
The PR's own motivation is two writers in separate processes sharing `MIMIR_HOME` (the in-process `asyncio.Lock` doesn't help cross-process). Sequence:
1. Process A: `_write_*` creates `INDEX.md.tmp.<pidA>.<hex>`, finishes `write_text`, not yet at `.replace()`.
2. Process B: enters `_write_*`, sweep globs + unlinks A's **live** tmp.
3. Process A: `tmp.replace(path)` → **FileNotFoundError** — the exact failure class #272 set out to remove.

The unique-name change alone already closes the original collision; the sweep then adds a narrower delete race on top. The docstring's "window is small" acknowledges it but doesn't close it. Guard the sweep, e.g.:
- only unlink tmps older than a threshold (`stat().st_mtime` older than N seconds), so a freshly-created live tmp is never swept; **or**
- skip tmps whose encoded PID is still alive; **or**
- drop the proactive sweep and clean only your *own* tmp in a `finally` (unique names already fix the original race; a startup-only sweep, when no writer can be running, mops up crash orphans).

Whichever you pick, add a test that a concurrently-created sibling `*.tmp.*` (simulating another process's in-flight write) is **not** swept.

### 2. (cleanup) Drop the stale pre-commit / sk- commits — rebase onto current main
This branch predates #479 (the `sk-proj[-_]` pre-commit fix), which has since merged to main — byte-identical final patterns. So the diff *looks* like it changes the hook, but post-merge it's a no-op, and the PR is carrying four unrelated chainlink-#237 commits. Rebase onto `origin/main` so this lands as a clean #272-only PR (`mimir/index.py` + `tests/test_index.py`); the pre-commit hunk should disappear.

CI is green and there's no hard git conflict, but #1 is a correctness regression under concurrent writers. Happy to re-review once the sweep is guarded + the branch rebased.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
Both points addressed.

**#1 (blocking) — orphan sweep now guards by PID liveness**

`_sweep_orphaned_tmps` parses the PID from each `.tmp.<pid>.<8-hex>` filename and probes it with `os.kill(pid, 0)` before unlinking:
- `ProcessLookupError` → PID dead → safe to unlink
- normal return → PID alive → in-flight tmp, skip
- `PermissionError` → PID exists but we can't signal it → treat as alive (conservative)
- name doesn't match the pattern → skip conservatively

This closes the race: a concurrent writer's tmp carries a live PID and is never swept.

New test added: `test_sweep_preserves_live_process_tmp` — encodes `os.getpid()` in a sibling filename and asserts the sweep leaves it alone.

Updated `test_sweep_removes_orphaned_tmps` to use a subprocess-spawned + waited PID so "dead" is provably dead, not probabilistic.

**#2 (cleanup) — rebased onto main**

Used `git rebase --onto origin/main fcbdfac HEAD` to replay only the two index commits (dropping the 4 stale pre-commit commits). Diff is now clean: `mimir/index.py` + `tests/test_index.py` only.

22/22 `tests/test_index.py` pass.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Both points addressed cleanly:
- **Sweep guard**: per-PID liveness via `os.kill(pid, 0)` — dead PID → unlink, alive/PermissionError → skip, unparseable name → skip. A concurrent writer's in-flight tmp is now protected, so the cross-process FileNotFoundError window is closed. The `unlink` is also race-wrapped. Solid.
- **Test**: `test_sweep_preserves_live_process_tmp` encodes the current (live) PID and asserts the tmp survives the sweep — exactly the missing coverage.
- **Rebased**: the stale #237 / pre-commit hunk is gone; this is now a clean #272-only PR.

CI green. Nice iteration.

Unifies four dashboards on the canonical `mimir.api_key` localStorage key. `saga_dashboard.html` and `file_memory_dashboard.html` had been using `mimir_api_key` (underscore) while `ops_dashboard.html` and `turn_viewer.html` used `mimir.api_key` (dot). payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: fix: tighten pre-commit sk- pattern to exclude hyphens

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Good instinct on the false-positive, but this trades it for a **secret-scan false-negative on `sk-proj-…` project keys** — which are OpenAI's default key format now.

**The regression.** `sk-[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}` (no hyphen) against a real project key `sk-proj-AbC…`:
- `sk-` matches, then `[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}` consumes `proj` (4 chars) and **stops at the `-`** → 4 < 20 → no match. The only `sk-` is at the start, so there's no later anchor either. The key is **not caught**.

**This contradicts our own code.** The runtime redactor in `mimir/git_bootstrap.py:136-139` documents these as `sk-proj-…` (hyphen) and keeps the hyphen in its class precisely to catch them:
```python
# OpenAI-style secret keys (``sk-…`` and ``sk-proj-…``)…
re.compile(r"sk-(?!ant-)[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}"),
```
So this PR's comment ("`sk-proj_…` which uses `_`") is at odds with the redactor, and after this change the pre-commit hook and the runtime redactor disagree on the same secret shape.

**Suggested fix** — kill the prose false-positive *and* keep project-key coverage by splitting into the two real shapes:
```sh
'sk-proj-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}'        # OpenAI project keys (hyphens/underscores in body)
'sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}'                # classic OpenAI keys (base62 — pure alphanumeric)
```
- A file path like `pask-approach-to-cybernetics` matches neither: it isn't `sk-proj-`, and the classic pattern needs 20+ *pure-alphanumeric* chars after `sk-`, but `approach` breaks at the first hyphen.
- Real classic keys (`sk-` + 48 base62) and project keys (`sk-proj-…`) are both still caught.

Worth a one-line note in the commit that this keeps parity with `git_bootstrap._TOKEN_PATTERNS`. Happy to re-review once it's split.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
You're right — good catch. `sk-[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}` stops at `proj` (4 chars) before hitting the `-` separator, so the 20-char minimum fails and the project key goes undetected.

Fixed with `sk-(?:proj-)?[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}`:
- Explicit `(?:proj-)?` infix allows the project-key prefix
- Body still requires 20+ non-hyphen chars — so wiki slugs like `sk-approach-to-...` still fail (body "approach" = 8 chars < 20)
- Pushed to branch, live hook updated to match.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
Addressed — split into two explicit patterns per the CR:

```sh
'sk-proj-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}'   # OpenAI project keys (body allows hyphens)
'sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}'            # OpenAI classic keys (base62 — no hyphens)
```

**Why the split works:**
- `sk-approach-to-cybernetics-1961` → doesn't start with `sk-proj-`, and classic pattern stops at the first hyphen in the body (`approach` = 8 chars < 20) → **no match ✓**
- `[REDACTED-CREDENTIAL]` → matches first pattern ✓
- `sk-AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUvWx` → matches second pattern ✓
- `sk-proj-AbC-Def-GhI-Jkl...` (body with hyphens) → matches first pattern ✓

**Parity with `git_bootstrap._TOKEN_PATTERNS`:** the two entries together cover the same key space as `sk-(?!ant-)[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}` — `sk-ant-` is already the separate entry above them, so the negative lookahead isn't needed here; the split is clearer than a single combined regex.

Live hook updated to match in the same commit. Rebased onto current main.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Addressed perfectly — thanks for the iteration.

The split is exactly right:
- `sk-proj-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}` catches OpenAI project keys (hyphens/underscores allowed in the body).
- `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` catches classic base62 keys and, because it allows no hyphens, won't fire on wiki slugs like `sk-foo-bar-…` (the run breaks at the first hyphen).
- `sk-ant-…` remains covered by its dedicated pattern above.

Project-key coverage is preserved and the original false-positive is gone. Approving — will merge once CI goes green.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Reversing my approve — CI caught a real regression, and it's on me: my earlier review said "use `sk-proj-` (hyphen)" but missed the pre-existing parity test `test_redact_and_pre_commit_hook_agree_on_openai_project_key` (chainlink #237), which pins the **underscore** form `sk-proj_…`.

**The failure** (pytest 3.11 + 3.12):
- Test candidate: `sk-proj_AbCdEfGh1234567890_ijKlMnOpQrSt` (underscore after `proj`).
- Runtime `_redact` (`sk-(?!ant-)[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}`) masks it ✓.
- New hook patterns miss it: `sk-proj-[…]` needs a literal hyphen (≠ `_`), and `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` stops at `proj` (4 chars) before the `_`. So the hook no longer refuses the commit → the "redact and hook agree" contract breaks.

**Fix** — accept either separator after `proj`:
```sh
'sk-proj[-_][A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}'     # OpenAI project keys (sk-proj- or sk-proj_; body may contain -/_)
'sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}'                # classic base62 keys (no hyphen → won't match slugs)
```
- `sk-proj_AbC…` → matched by line 1 (the `[-_]` covers the `_`). Parity restored.
- `sk-proj-AbC…` (real hyphen keys) → also matched by line 1.
- `pask-approach-to-…` / `sk-foo-bar` → matched by neither (not `sk-proj[-_]`; classic breaks at the first hyphen). False-positive still gone.

Run `pytest tests/test_git_bootstrap_redact.py -q` to confirm green before re-requesting. Sorry for the misdirection on the separator.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: fix(git): stop credential.helper + safe.directory accumulating every container boot

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
This is a clean, well-scoped fix for two accumulation bugs. Both root causes are accurately diagnosed and the fixes are mechanically correct.

## credential.helper (`git_bootstrap.py`)

The `--replace-all` change is exactly right. The previous bare `git config --local credential.helper ""` fails with *"cannot overwrite multiple values with a single value"* once the key is multi-valued — it neither clears nor errors loudly enough to be actionable, so the subsequent `--add` silently stacks another `store` entry every boot. `--replace-all` atomically collapses any number of existing values to the single empty, making the `["", "store --file=..."]` pair a fixed point. The comment in the code explains the reasoning well.

No credential-flow risk: the semantics are identical to what was intended on first boot — empty entry to suppress inherited helpers, then `store` entry. The only difference is it now reliably achieves that on every boot rather than just the first.

## safe.directory (`scaffold_docker.py`)

The `get-all | grep -qxF || --add` guard is idiomatically correct:
- `-F` (fixed-string) avoids regex interpretation of path characters.
- `-x` (whole-line match) prevents a path like `/workspace/mimir` from matching `/workspace/mimir-fork`.
- `-q` keeps output clean.
- `2>/dev/null` on the `git config --get-all` correctly suppresses the exit-1 + no-output case when the key is entirely absent, and the `||` chain is safe under `set -euo pipefail` because a command followed by `||` suppresses `errexit` for that expression.

The check runs before `cd "${REPO_DIR}"` is not needed — the guard reads `$REPO_DIR` which is already set, so placement after the `cd` is fine.

## Tests

Both tests are well-targeted:
- `test_credential_helper_idempotent_across_bootstraps`: runs bootstrap 3× against a real git repo and asserts the helper list is exactly `["", "store --file=..."]` — directly catches the accumulation regression.
- `test_workspace_start_sh_guards_safe_directory`: structural assertion on the raw template string. For a bash template embedded in Python this is a pragmatic approach; it will catch removal of the guard without requiring a shell execution harness.

## Minor observations (non-blocking)

- The scaffold test (`test_workspace_start_sh_guards_safe_directory`) imports `_START_SH_TEMPLATE` (the workspace template, not pypi). That's the right template. The pypi template never had this path, which matches the PR description's observation that pypi-mode was unaffected.
- No concurrent-boot concern: `git config --global --add` is the only writer and it's guarded by the read-check; a race between two simultaneous boots could add a duplicate, but that's an inherent TOCTOU of the shell check, and in practice start.sh runs sequentially (a single container entrypoint). Acceptable.
- Self-healing for existing 273-entry configs: `--replace-all` correctly collapses the accumulated entries on the next bootstrap — no manual scrub needed. Correct.

Approved. Solid fix with good test coverage.
