payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: feat(feedback): resolved-incident filter to silence fixed errors (chainlink #197)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approve. Clean filter-side implementation of the resolved-incident feature from chainlink #197 — closes the noisiest part of the original problem (post-fix events lingering in the feedback block for the full 24h window).

## What works

- **`_is_event_resolved` is composable.** Three independent match axes (type / pattern / timestamp) AND-combined. Each axis has a default-permissive degenerate case (`"*"` wildcard for type, empty pattern matches all of a type, missing `resolved_at` skips the rule) — operator can use exactly as much specificity as they need.
- **Lazy `json.dumps(ev)`** for pattern matching — only serialises the event when a rule actually has a non-empty pattern. Zero-cost in the common case (no rules / no patterns).
- **Substring match against the full JSON** is the right cheap-and-cheerful choice. Covers nested fields without needing per-shape match strategies; paired with `event_type` filtering it's bounded enough to avoid noisy false positives.
- **Loaded fresh on every `recent()` call** — no caching pitfall where an in-flight rule edit doesn't take effect until restart. The cost is one JSONL read per call, which is dwarfed by the events.jsonl tail-read in the same path.
- **Defensive `_load_resolved_incidents`** — bad JSON lines skipped, OSError swallowed to empty list. The file is operator-curated, so corruption from a half-write or a stray `cat` won't break feedback.
- **Test coverage hits the load-bearing properties**: suppression fires for matching, doesn't fire for post-fix events (the timestamp axis), type mismatch doesn't suppress, `*` wildcard works, no file is a graceful no-op.

## Observations (non-blocking)

- **No CLI for writing entries yet.** Chainlink #197 sketched `mimir feedback mark-resolved --type error --pattern X --reason Y` as the operator surface. This PR delivers the consumer side; without the writer side, the operator has to hand-craft JSONL lines (`echo '{...}' >> $MIMIR_HOME/resolved-incidents.jsonl`). Doable but error-prone, and easy to typo the ISO timestamp shape. Worth a follow-on chainlink for the CLI — not blocking this PR, but the feature is incomplete without it.
- **Timestamp comparison is string-based.** Both `ev_ts` and `rule_resolved_at` are compared lexicographically. Correct as long as both are in the same ISO-8601 format (timezone-suffixed). An operator writing `resolved_at: "2026-05-25T19:30:00"` (no `+00:00`) would compare unexpectedly against `event_ts: "2026-05-25T19:10:00+00:00"`. Worth either (a) a docstring callout requiring tz-suffixed timestamps, or (b) parsing both via `datetime.fromisoformat()` for robustness. The CLI in the followup PR would naturally enforce this by defaulting to `datetime.now(tz=UTC).isoformat()`.
- **Pattern false-positive scope is bounded but not zero.** A pattern of `"discord"` would match the same string appearing in any event's `channel_id`. Paired with `event_type` filtering this is fine in practice, but a `"event_type": "*"` rule with a loose pattern could silently mask unrelated signals. Worth a note in the eventual user-facing docs ("be specific with type when you can").

The CLI gap is the only thing meaningful enough to warrant a follow-up. Tests are solid for what's shipped.

Ship it.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: fix(bash_async): wrapper-invariant guard via prefix + URI suffix key (chainlink #192)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approve. Substantive, well-designed extension of the #356 guard. Hits the chainlink #192 spec on both axes (wrapper-invariance + truncation) and the OR-semantics design is the right call.

## What works

- **Two-key match is the right shape.** Prefix-key (after normalisation) OR suffix-key (rightmost URI) — either signal alone is sufficient evidence of same-intent. Conservative on false-negatives, with a built-in escape hatch for false-positives (suffix-key returns ``None`` for commands without a URI, so non-URI workflows like ``git fetch origin`` aren't affected).
- **Pipeline composition in ``_intent_prefix``.** Four discrete steps (unwrap shell wrapper → take last chain segment → strip env-exports → basename-normalise executable). Each is independently testable; each handles a different sub-pattern of the 14:04 retry escalation.
- **Basename normalisation closes the case-4 escape.** ``/usr/bin/node cli.js dispatch …`` → ``node cli.js dispatch …`` matches the bare ``node`` form. Worth flagging that this is what makes the suffix-key fallback rarely-needed in practice — most case-4 escalations land in the prefix-key match once basename-normed.
- **``match_kind`` in the refusal string** is the right observability touch — operators auditing refusal patterns can grep by which signal fired, separating ``prefix`` matches (the common case) from ``uri-target`` matches (the bail-out for unusual wrappers).
- **MAX_CHARS bumped 100 → 200**: addresses the truncation-collision concern from the #356 review. The longer window absorbs the typical command body without hitting the cap.

## Observations (non-blocking)

- **``_take_last_chain_segment`` is naïve about ``&&`` inside quoted arguments.** ``echo 'foo && bar' && cleanup`` would split into ``["echo 'foo ", " bar' ", " cleanup"]`` and pick ``cleanup``. The agent's bash_async usage is overwhelmingly straightforward chains (no quoted-string args containing ``&&``), so this is a real edge case but not a practical one. Worth a one-line docstring note rather than a fix.
- **``_intent_suffix_key`` URI matching is greedy on query strings.** ``\S+`` will capture trailing ``?p=v&q=z`` so two invocations differing only in tracking params won't match via the URI key. Likely fine — AT-URIs and direct API endpoints rarely have variable query strings in this codepath; if it becomes a problem, a normalisation pass (strip query string) is cheap to add later.
- **``_unwrap_shell_wrapper`` quote handling uses ``rfind``.** Catches the common case (``bash -c 'cmd "with quotes" arg'``) but would close-early on a body with a literal apostrophe before the closing quote. Unlikely in practice; the agent's shell wrappers don't typically use single quotes inside single-quoted bodies.

None of these are blocking — the guard is strictly better than #356's version for every observed retry pattern, and the failure modes flagged here are agent-behaviour shapes that haven't been seen in production.

Ship it.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: feat(feedback): emit algedonic event when bash_async guard refuses same-intent respawn (chainlink #193)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approve. Closes the observability gap the original guard left.

## What works

- **``safe_log_event`` (not ``log_event``)** is the right choice for a tool-side emit. Bench runners + tests don't initialise the event logger; using the safe variant means the guard fires cleanly regardless.
- **Payload shape is right** — ``channel_id``, ``running_job_id``, truncated ``new_command``, ``intent_prefix``. Enough for forensics + dashboards without leaking full command bodies (which could contain secrets in env-export retries).
- **Renderer + ``_EVENT_RULES`` entry**: surfaces in the algedonic block in a form the agent can act on (\"I tried to respawn a job and was refused — investigate the existing one before retrying\").

## Observations (non-blocking)

- **Single test feels light** for a feature that closes an observability hole, but the seam being tested (emit-via-monkeypatch) is the load-bearing one. The existing refusal-shape tests in this file cover the guard fires correctly; this PR's test pins the new event-emission contract. Fine as-is.
- **Refusal still returns the same string** to the agent — no agent-visible behaviour change. Pure additive event. That's the right scope for an observability PR.

Ship it.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: fix(feedback): informative renderers for poller circuit-breaker events (chainlink #196)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approve. Clever use of an existing mechanism (content-level dedup in ``build_feedback_block``) to solve the per-tick spam problem, without adding new dedup logic.

## What works

- **Content-stability-as-dedup-key is the right design.** Omitting ``remaining_seconds`` from the rendered string is the load-bearing choice — it turns 5 suppressed-run events for the same poller during a single 5-minute backoff into ONE dedup'd entry with a count, rather than five lines that look like an escalating crisis.
- **Per-poller identity is preserved.** Different pollers in their own circuit-breaker states surface separately (the second test pins this), so the dedup doesn't blur signals.
- **Test coverage exactly matches the dedup invariants.** Same-poller-collapses-to-one + different-pollers-surface-separately + tripped-renderer-includes-name. Three tests, three load-bearing properties.

## Observations (non-blocking)

- **ETA info is lost from the rendered string.** ``remaining_seconds`` is in the raw event payload but not in the algedonic block. The agent can still know "this is still suppressing" from the dedup'd entry but not "for how long." That's the right tradeoff for the algedonic surface (which is for decision-making, not exact-timing), and the raw event is available via ``events.jsonl`` if anything needs the ETA. Worth a one-line comment in the renderer explaining the omission is deliberate, so a future maintainer doesn't "fix" it back.

Ship it.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: fix(skills/weather): invoke via python3 -m so the path resolves regardless of cwd

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Review: fix(skills/weather) — invoke via python3 -m

**Verdict: Approve ✅**

### What this does

Switches all SKILL.md invocation examples from `python3 skills/weather/get_weather.py` (a relative path that fails from any realistic cwd) to `python3 -m mimir.skills.weather.get_weather` (resolves via `sys.path`, cwd-independent). Also adds the new module-path glob to `success_criteria.any_of` while keeping the legacy `*get_weather.py*` matcher.

### Correctness

- **Fix is correct.** The `-m` invocation delegates path resolution to Python's import system rather than the shell's cwd — the right approach for a script that can live in a venv, an editable install, or a built wheel. All four deployment shapes listed in the PR description will resolve correctly as long as the `mimir` package is importable, which it must be for the agent to be running at all.
- **`success_criteria` update is correct.** New glob is added first in `any_of`; old glob retained for backward compat. The comment update ("works from any cwd") accurately describes the behavior.
- **No false-negative risk.** The legacy `*get_weather.py*` glob stays, so any agent still using a direct path invocation still gets credit. The new glob covers the documented invocation going forward.

### Minor observations (non-blocking)

- **Comment cleanup (cosmetic):** The old inline comment read `"run get_weather.py"` — updated to `"run get_weather"`. Good.
- **Operator-override snapshots:** PR correctly scopes this as out-of-scope (snapshots update on rebuild). The in-place patch note in the PR body is the right mitigation for existing deployments without rebuild.
- **Legacy glob longevity:** The `*get_weather.py*` success_criteria entry can be dropped in a future PR once the old invocation shape is fully deprecated, but keeping it now is the conservative correct call.

### What's not changed (confirmed correct)

- `get_weather.py` itself — untouched, works in both invocation styles.
- Frontmatter shape — skill-conformance tests unaffected.

The problem is demonstrated concretely (0/7 successful invocations on muninn, 3 days of bad path guesses), the fix is minimal and surgical, and the verification is real. Ship it.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: fix(turn-viewer): preserve scroll position of inner event-bdy boxes across 5s polls

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
**Verdict: Approve** ✅

## Summary

Extends the existing outer-panel scroll preservation (lines 510-605) to cover the independently-scrollable `.event-bdy` inner boxes. The implementation is a direct and consistent application of the same pattern already used in the file.

## What's good

- **Pattern consistency.** `captureEventBdyScrolls` / `restoreEventBdyScrolls` mirror the outer-panel `savedScrollTop` + `requestAnimationFrame` shape exactly. Anyone reading the existing scroll code will immediately understand the new code.
- **`requestAnimationFrame` is correct here.** Same rationale as the outer-panel rAF at line 604 — the DOM needs one layout pass before `scrollTop` assignments stick. No reason to diverge.
- **Index-based key is the right choice.** Events always append at end, so the index of any existing box is stable across polls. A freshly-arrived event gets scrollTop=0 by default, which is the correct UX.
- **Null guards are tight.** `captureEventBdyScrolls` returns `[]` on null container; `restoreEventBdyScrolls` exits early on empty-array saved state. No crashes from edge cases.
- **`isRefresh` gate is correct.** First open of a new turn starts all boxes at top — matching the outer-panel behavior.
- **Both render paths covered.** The `canInterleave` combined list and the legacy split-saga layout both get the capture/restore wrapping.

## Minor observations (non-blocking)

- The `saved[i] > 0` skip in the restore loop avoids a no-op assignment for top-aligned boxes. That's fine, but it also means a box that was scrolled down and then manually reset to the top during the 5s window won't be "locked" at 0 — it'll re-render at whatever position the new innerHTML produces, which is 0 anyway. No behavioral difference; just noting the semantics.
- The PR correctly calls out no automated tests. Given that `.event-bdy` scroll preservation is only observable against live polling + real content exceeding 360px, this is the right call.

No changes requested.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
Verdict: **APPROVE**

## Summary

Pure JS fix to  — captures  scrollTop values before each 5-second poll's  replace, restores them after. Addresses a real usability friction (long reasoning blocks scroll-jumping on every poll).

## Observations

**Correct on all the load-bearing details:**

- Index-within-container as the restoration key is sound — new events always append at the end in both layout branches, so existing indices stay stable. Newly arrived events default to scrollTop=0, which is the right UX.
- `isRefresh ? captureEventBdyScrolls(...) : []` guard: first-open of a different turn correctly starts every box at the top; only refreshes of the same turn preserve scroll state.
- `requestAnimationFrame` for restore: same rationale as the existing outer-panel restore at lines 597-607 — necessary to wait for the browser to commit the new layout before `scrollTop` assignment, else it silently no-ops against the layout pass.
- `Math.min(boxes.length, saved.length)` handles the edge case where new events arrive mid-stream: only restores positions for boxes that existed before the render. Correct.
- `if (saved[i] > 0)` optimization is fine — avoids a no-op assignment when the box was already at the top.

**Null guards on both helpers** — both handle missing containers cleanly.

**Three call sites covered** — combined layout + both sub-paths in the legacy layout. Complete.

**No test comment** is reasonable given this requires live frontend + polling to verify, and the fix is a direct mirror of the existing outer-panel pattern that already shipped without a test harness.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: feat(index): auto-regenerate skills-catalog.md on memory flush (chainlink #109)

payload.author: jasoncarreira

Approve. Closes a real drift gap — `memory/skills-catalog.md` is loaded into every turn's prompt, so stale descriptions cost real tokens AND mislead the agent's skill-selection logic.

Observations:

- **Diff-before-write** keeps disk/index churn down — good for systems that watch the file's mtime (e.g., the bind-mount-health-probe).
- **`skills_root` test injection point** is the right seam — tests get a deterministic root without monkeypatching, production path stays unchanged.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: feat(pollers): circuit-breaker — suspend after 3 consecutive failures (chainlink #94)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approve. Standard circuit-breaker pattern (closed → open → half-open via first clean run), well-scoped to pollers, with the right algedonic signal shape.

Observations:

- **`poller_circuit_tripped` fires once / `poller_circuit_open` fires on each suppressed run** — correct separation: the trip is a state transition (rare, attention-worthy), the open is a per-tick "still suppressing" log (useful for dashboards but not noisy in the algedonic surface if the rules in `feedback.py` weight it appropriately — worth checking that downstream).
- **The autouse `clear_circuit_breakers` fixture** is the right call. Module-level state bleeding across tests is exactly the kind of thing that produces flaky tests when run in different orders.
- **Auto-reset on first clean run** matches operator intuition — if I fix a poller's config and it succeeds, I don't want to wait out the backoff timer.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: fix(commitments): warn once when store event count exceeds scale threshold (chainlink #106)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:

- **Per-instance `_warned_large_store` flag** prevents the warning from spamming the log on every poller-sweep `current_state()` call. Good — a warning-per-call would be worse than no warning at all.
- **500-event threshold** is arbitrary but documented (module constant); fine to tune later.
- **Test for per-instance independence** is the kind of test that catches "oh, I made it a class-var instead of an instance-var" regressions. Nice.

payload.author: mimir-carreira

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approve. Two real bugs in one PR:

1. **`recipient_identity` was always None** — extracted commitments could never @-mention anyone, even when the LLM clearly surfaced a recipient.
2. **Dedupe-key collision across recipients** — "remind Alice about X" and "remind Bob about X" silently collapsed into one commitment record. That's a correctness bug, not just an ergonomic one.

The fix is straight-line: extract → coerce → thread through dedupe_key. Tests cover both the happy path and the null/empty/whitespace handling (which is exactly where you'd get a silent regression if the coerce step gets refactored).

Observations:

payload.author: mimir-carreira

Two things worth specifically calling out:

- **Value NOT logged in the event payload** — correct. The whole point is to flag the misconfiguration; logging the value would defeat it.
- **`MIMIR_*` prefix is in the deny list** — good catch. Internal mimir env vars (`MIMIR_API_KEY`, etc.) hardcoded into `poller.env` would be the worst kind of slip.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: test(skill-conformance): enforce <!-- desc: --> first-body-line on all SKILL.md files (chainlink #102)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: fix(bash_async): wait-on-pending guard — refuse same-intent respawns (chainlink #189)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approve. Targets the exact retry-respawn pattern observed in turn 201c (chainlink #189), with a focused per-channel guard and a refusal message that tells the operator what to do next.

## What works

- **`_intent_prefix()` skip-list matches the observed pattern** — leading `export`-keyword and bare `VAR=val` tokens are exactly what the agent kept tweaking between retries.
- **Per-channel scope** is the right boundary — unrelated channels don't block each other, but the same agent in a runaway loop on one channel is restrained.
- **Refusal text is actionable** — naming the running `job_id` + pointing at `bash_job_output` gives the agent (and any operator reading the log) a clear next step instead of just "no."
- **Tests pin both axes** — 5 unit tests cover `_intent_prefix` normalization, 5 integration tests cover the guard's allow/refuse decisions across channel, running-state, and intent variants.

## Observations (non-blocking)

- **Wrapper invariance is partial.** The guard catches `social-cli ...` vs `export FOO=bar social-cli ...` cleanly. It does NOT catch `social-cli ...` vs `/bin/bash -c 'social-cli ...'` — different leading tokens, different prefix. Turn 201c eventually shifted from direct `social-cli` invocations to `/bin/bash -c '... node /mimir-home/.local/social-cli/dist/cli.js ...'` wrappings. Those would still slip through. Worth a docstring note (the existing docstring already says "Intent equality is heuristic" — could add an example of a wrapper variant that escapes the match). Not blocking — partial coverage of a runaway pattern is strictly better than none, and the wrapper-invariance case is a follow-on, not this PR.
- **100-char truncation** could collide for genuinely-different commands sharing a long prefix (`git fetch ... --opt-a` vs `git fetch ... --opt-b` where the divergence lands past char 100). For the observed failure mode this is fine; flag for `_intent_prefix` docstring.
- **Recovery path**: when the refusal fires, the agent gets a string return — no algedonic event. Consider emitting `bash_async_refused_same_intent` (negative) so the algedonic surface picks it up alongside other refusals. Separate PR; not for this one.

Ship it.

## Review: test(hooks): mock companion that runs without claude CLI auth

**Verdict: Approve** — clean follow-up, sound coverage rationale, well-implemented.

---

### What this does

Adds two `@pytest.mark.asyncio` mock tests that exercise the hook-pairing contract directly (no subprocess, no auth, no network), filling the gap that `#354`'s skip-when-unauthenticated approach left in CI and fresh-contributor environments:

- **`test_hooks_capture_built_in_bash_tool_mocked`** — two sequential Bash invocations, verifies pre/post pairing by `tool_use_id`, ordering invariant, and `is_error=False` on the success path
- **`test_hooks_capture_failure_path_mocked`** — PostToolUseFailure path, pins `is_error=True` + `error` discriminator that turn-logger / algedonic surfacing depend on

Zero production code changes.

---

### Observations

**Good:**

- The layered coverage model is correctly reasoned: mocks pin the hook-side contract (always), integration test pins the SDK-side wiring (when possible). The PR description table makes this explicit and is a useful reference for future readers.
- `try/finally` around `_tool_events_var.set/reset` is the right shape — cleanup is guaranteed even if assertions raise.
- Using two distinct `tool_use_id`s (`toolu_01` / `toolu_02`) and asserting `set(by_id.keys()) == {"toolu_01", "toolu_02"}` correctly rules out cross-id aliasing, not just sequence-position coincidence.
- The ordering assertion (`["tool_call", "tool_result"]` per id) is a genuine invariant to pin — good catch.
- Failure-path test is a real coverage win; the integration test can't reliably exercise `PostToolUseFailure` without a model-on-cue failing tool invocation.
- Error messages in assertions include the actual data, which is the right pattern for test diagnostics.

**Non-blocking observations:**

- The failure-path test asserts `len(events) == 2` (exact count) rather than the more relaxed "at least one of each type." The exact-count form is fine here since the mock drives the exact sequence — just worth noting it's an intentional choice, not a looser assertion that accidentally passes.
- The success-path test uses a separate `by_id_order` dict for the ordering check, which re-traverses `bash_events`. Could be collapsed into the `by_id` loop, but readability wins at this size — no suggestion to change.
- The docstring in `test_hooks_capture_built_in_bash_tool_mocked` is thorough enough that it doubles as a design doc for the layered strategy. That's a feature, not a problem.

---

### Test output consistency

PR description shows `19 passed` (authed) / `18 passed, 1 skipped` (no-auth). The arithmetic is correct: 17 pre-existing + 2 new = 19 authed; integration skips → 18 + 1 skipped. Consistent.

---

No changes requested. Good follow-through on closing the coverage gap.

payload.title: test: skip ClaudeSDKClient integration test when CLI cannot auth (chainlink #191)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approve. Right call to convert a misleading assertion failure into a clean skip.

## What works

- **Probe captures the actual failure mode.** The previous `_claude_cli_available` check only verified the binary existed; this one verifies it can complete a request, which is what the integration test actually needs. The diagnostic difference — `expected Bash tool to fire hooks; got events for: []` vs `SKIPPED [claude CLI ... cannot make API calls]` — is a substantial improvement for anyone debugging a CI run.
- **Cheapest possible probe.** Single-word "ok" prompt with `--output-format text`; minimal tokens, single round-trip, capped at 30s.
- **Probe-at-collection-time is fine.** The docstring's note about deliberately not caching is correct — `skipif` evaluates once per session anyway, so a session-level cache would be premature optimization.

## Observations (non-blocking)

- **One real tension** worth naming, not blocking: in a properly-authenticated environment the probe makes an actual API call against quota just to decide whether to run the test. Cost is trivial (single short prompt), but it's a side effect of test collection — worth a one-line callout in the docstring if anyone wonders "why did `pytest --collect-only` hit Anthropic." Not a fix for this PR; just a note.
- **Coverage tradeoff**: this hides a real integration gap behind a skip in unauthenticated environments (CI, fresh contributors). The right long-term shape is splitting the hook-coverage assertions into a unit test with a mock `ClaudeSDKClient` (so the contract is checked everywhere) and keeping this one as an auth-gated smoke. Chainlink #191 closes with this fix; a follow-on chainlink for the unit-test extraction would be reasonable but isn't this PR's job.

Ship it.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Adding a follow-up commit on this branch (`dc0a825`) per operator request — extends the PR to also close the coverage gap that the original skip-when-unauthenticated approach left behind.

## The gap the skip-only approach leaves

The integration test guarantees "the SDK actually calls our hooks." Important, but it has a structural cost: in environments without claude CLI auth (CI, fresh contributors, sandboxed dev containers) the test silently skips, and the hook-pairing contract gets **zero coverage** there. A regression that broke `_pre_tool_use_hook` or `_post_tool_use_hook` would slip through CI undetected.

## The layered shape the follow-up commit introduces

Three layers, each pinning a different slice of the system:

| Layer | What it pins | When it runs |
|---|---|---|
| **Mock tests** (new) | hook-side contract: given the SDK's documented call pattern, our hooks produce paired events with consistent `tool_use_id` | always |
| **Integration test** (unchanged from this PR) | SDK-side wiring: the SDK *actually* calls our hooks at the right times for built-in tools | when claude CLI is authed |
| **Earlier unit tests** (untouched) | hook plumbing internals (contextvar lifecycle, idempotent install, etc.) | always |

The mocks are deliberately not a replacement for the integration test — they trust the SDK's documented contract. If Anthropic ever changes that contract, *only* the integration test will catch it. But the existing-and-always-skipping baseline was strictly weaker than "trust the SDK contract here, verify it elsewhere."

## What the new tests cover

- **`test_hooks_capture_built_in_bash_tool_mocked`**: simulates two Bash invocations (distinct `tool_use_id`s), runs the same assertions the integration test runs (pairing, ordering, `is_error=False` on success) against the simulated stream.
- **`test_hooks_capture_failure_path_mocked`**: covers the `PostToolUseFailure` path that the integration test doesn't reliably exercise (would need the model to invoke a failing tool on cue). Pins the `is_error=True` + `error` discriminator that turn-logger + algedonic surfacing depend on.

## Verified locally

```
$ uv run pytest tests/test_langchain_claude_code_patches.py -q
19 passed, 3 warnings in 14.57s
```

(Integration test included — this machine has claude CLI auth. The two new mocks run sub-second on their own.)

Net diff: this commit adds ~136 lines of test, zero production code change.

Approve. Tight, test-only PR that fills a documented-but-untested case.

## What works

The production try/except can move within `turn_hooks.py` without breaking this test, which is exactly what you want.

payload.title: fix(asyncio): hold strong refs for fire-and-forget create_task callers (chainlink #118)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approve. Solid execution of a textbook bug-class fix — the cpython-documented strong-ref pattern, applied at the three sites grep-able by `loop.create_task(...)` with the return discarded. Notes are nits; nothing blocking.

## What works

- **Pattern is correctly applied at all three sites**: each callsite uses the canonical shape — `tasks.add(task)` + `task.add_done_callback(tasks.discard)` — so the set stays bounded to in-flight tasks rather than growing unbounded.
- **`_spawn()` helper in scheduler.py centralizes the dance**, so any future fire-and-forget site in scheduler picks up the pattern by default instead of re-inventing it.
- **Tests pin the contract both ways**: ref held while in-flight, removed after completion. The `log_started`/`log_unblocked` event-pair pattern is exactly the right way to wedge the task into a suspended state for assertion — and the inline note about the two `await asyncio.sleep(0)` yields (one for the task, one for the `call_soon`-scheduled discard callback) is the kind of comment that pays for itself the next time someone debugs this test.
- **Every site references the cpython docs callout** in its comment, so future grep will land readers on the explanation, not just the workaround.

## Observations (non-blocking)

- **Instance-level vs module-level `_background_tasks` differs by file**: scheduler keeps it per-`Scheduler` instance (right call — tests instantiate multiple schedulers, and per-instance keeps test isolation); budget.py and budget_gate.py keep it module-level (also right — both are de-facto singletons). The mixed shape is correct, but it'd be worth one line in `_spawn`'s docstring noting why scheduler chose per-instance, since a reader following the pattern to a new fire-and-forget site could pick the wrong shape.

- **`_spawn(coro: Awaitable[Any], ...)`**: `loop.create_task()` is documented to accept coroutines specifically (not all `Awaitable`s). The wider type hint compiles but a future strict-mypy pass would complain. Tightening to `Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]` would match what the call actually requires.

- **Two `asyncio.get_running_loop()` calls per dispatch**: the outer `try/except RuntimeError` confirms a loop exists, then `_spawn` re-acquires the loop internally. Functionally fine (`get_running_loop` is cheap and the outer check is the no-loop fallback path), but if you wanted to DRY it you could pass `loop` into `_spawn`. Not worth changing.

- **Discord/Slack bridge `_safe_log_event` sites correctly scoped out** per the PR body. Agreed — those run inside an exception handler in supervisor loops, so the failure mode is different and warrants a separate review.

- **Test doesn't exercise the actual GC race** (which would require disabling the strong ref and inducing a collection — fragile, implementation-coupled). It tests the contract instead: "ref held during the task's lifetime, removed after." That's the right test shape; trust the cpython docs that GC is what depends on this contract.

Nice catch on the fleet-wide cleanup approach rather than per-PR patches.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Approve. Clean fail-loud fix for the silent-swallow gotcha. Notes below are observations, not blockers.

## What works

- **State machine is right**: `in_folded_block` flips on at `key: >` / `key: |`, off at any zero-indent key match (since `_KEY_RE` is anchored at `^`, an indented `foo: bar` won't terminate the block — correct YAML behavior).
- **Error message is useful**: names the offending key + shows the malformed line. Author lands on the fix immediately.
- **Empty-line handling**: blank lines inside a folded block hit `raw.strip()` falsy and fall through all branches → ignored, matching YAML semantics. No regression risk for skill files with paragraph breaks in `description: >`.
- **Backward-compat preserved**: the trailing `elif not in_folded_block and current_key is not None and raw.strip()` keeps the old legacy plain-value continuation path alive untouched.

## Observations (non-blocking)

- **Test coverage is exactly the two cases that mattered**: zero-indent key terminates (the swallow path), and non-indented non-key raises. Could add a "consecutive folded blocks" case (`key1: >\n  a\nkey2: >\n  b`) for completeness, but the state-flip logic in the key branch already covers it and the existing onboarding/SKILL.md regression test indirectly exercises it.
- **Branch ordering matters**: the `elif _KEY_RE.match(raw)` check sits *before* the in-folded-block continuation checks, which is what makes the "next key terminates the block" behavior correct. Worth a comment if anyone refactors this later, but the test is the load-bearing doc here.
- **Pre-existing edge case unchanged**: `description: > hint` (value-after-marker) won't enter folded mode (`value in {">", "|"}` is exact). Not introduced by this PR; flagging only because it's adjacent.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: fix: review-nits follow-up (PRs #342, #344, #345)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Review — PR #346 (review-nits follow-up for #342, #344, #345)

Clean bundle overall. All three nits are addressed correctly and the test coverage is appropriate. One real issue and a couple of minor observations.

### Real issue — `scheduler.py`: redundant `import traceback as _tb`

`scheduler.py` already imports `traceback` at module level (line 30):
```python
import traceback as tb
```
The PR adds `import traceback as _tb` **inside each `except` block** of `_consolidate()`. This:
- Duplicates the existing module-level import
- Introduces a second alias (`_tb`) that shadows the established `tb` alias used elsewhere in the file

Fix: drop both in-body imports and use the existing `tb` alias:
```python
except SagaError as exc:
    await log_event(
        "saga_consolidate_error",
        error=str(exc),
        status=exc.status,
        traceback=tb.format_exc(),
    )
except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
    await log_event(
        "saga_consolidate_error",
        error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
        traceback=tb.format_exc(),
    )
```
(The `_tb` alias was presumably chosen to avoid visually shadowing the `traceback=` keyword argument, but the module-level `tb` alias sidesteps that concern cleanly.)

---

### Minor observations

**`client.py` — warning placement is correct.** The warnings fire unconditionally when the unsupported params are passed, including on `dry_run=True` calls. That's the right behaviour — callers exploring the API surface with a dry-run should see the gap too.

**`test_commitments_extractor.py` — dual assertion is a nice touch.** The explicit UTC equivalence check (`10am EST == 15:00 UTC`) makes the intent human-readable and would catch an off-by-sign error in the offset.

**`test_saga_store.py` — three separate `SagaStore` instantiations.** Could share a fixture, but test clarity > DRY for unit tests at this scale; acceptable as-is.

**`test_scheduler.py` — `_RaisingSagaClient` pattern is consistent** with the `commitments_due_check_error` test already in the file. `_reset_logger_for_tests()` in `finally` is correct.

---

### Summary

One real fix needed (drop the redundant in-body `import traceback as _tb` in favour of the existing `tb` alias). Everything else is solid. The test coverage on all three nits is exactly right.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: feat: auto-inject channel memory into per-turn prompt (chainlink #187)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Submitting as a comment-only review (no approve/changes-requested) because the code is fine but the deployment decision is for Jason, not me.

## Code (would approve in isolation)

Clean implementation:
- ``load_channel_memory()`` walks ``<home>/memory/channels/<channel_id>/*.md``, concatenates, caps at ~8 KB with UTF-8-safe truncation and a visible "[truncated]" marker so the agent sees the loss rather than silently missing tail content.
- Synthetic channels (``scheduler:*``, ``poller:*``) correctly excluded.
- Wrapped in ``asyncio.to_thread()`` at the agent.py call site — bounded file I/O off the loop.
- Prompt placement after identity reconciliation + before algedonic feedback — correct "WHO before WHAT happened" ordering.
- 9 new tests across ``test_core_blocks.py`` + ``test_prompts.py``. Injection path verified; omission-for-synthetic-channels verified.

## Policy concern (the actual gate)

This is the change from the conversation we had earlier today on the propose/approve framework. The mechanism mechanically moves channel-memory writes from "autonomous, opt-in fetch" to "autonomous, auto-injected every turn" — that gives them the same compounding-cost / silent-self-modification footprint that core blocks have. Per the tri-zone model in ``persona-spec-framework`` + ``06-action-boundaries.md``, that's an escalate-first action category, not autonomous.

The PR body says: *"Coupled part 2 (zone justification in memory/core/06-action-boundaries.md) already shipped in state repo"* with a rationale of "per-channel blast radius is bounded (affects only that channel's turns, not globally)."

**That rationale is defensible** — per-channel scope IS smaller than global core. But the question for Jason is whether that bounded blast radius is enough to keep channel writes in the autonomous zone, OR whether channel writes should also move to escalate-first to match the new downside profile.

This isn't a code review question. It's the framework-application question the conversation surfaced earlier. The harness PR shouldn't land until:
1. Jason confirms he's comfortable with channel writes staying autonomous after the mechanism change, OR
2. The action-boundaries policy gets a corresponding update to move channel writes to escalate-first

Linking the state-repo commit for ``06-action-boundaries.md`` would help — operators reviewing this from the outside can't see the rationale otherwise.

Holding the merge for Jason's call.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
One more thing before merge — the `DEFAULT_ACTION_BOUNDARIES` scaffold template in `mimir/cli.py:854` (the constant `setup` writes to `memory/core/06-action-boundaries.md` on fresh installs) needs the same zone justification we added to my state repo. Right now the template's "File operations" section only talks about `memory/core/` and `memory/` (non-core) generically. After this PR lands, every PyPI install will start auto-injecting `memory/channels/<id>/*.md` into every turn prompt on that channel — but the boundaries file the agent reads won't explain *why* writes there stay autonomous.

Could you add a bullet to the "File operations" section of `DEFAULT_ACTION_BOUNDARIES`, something like:

```

  **autonomous**. These files are auto-injected into every turn

  not globally like ``memory/core/`` does.
```

Wording can flex — the points to land are (1) the path, (2) that it auto-injects, (3) the bounded-blast-radius justification for the autonomous zone. Same reasoning already documented in the `core_blocks.py` module-level comment in this PR; this just gets it into the scaffold so new installs ship with it.

Two clean fixes + one explicit deferral. Worth approving but two observations.

**What's right (approve):**

1. **``contribution_threshold`` / ``contradiction_threshold`` silently dropped at the in-process layer.** The HTTP path forwards them; in-process accepts the params but ignores them. 2. **Scope creep — is the loop_detector sliding-window change really also in this PR?** The subagent review I ran reported finding loop_detector.py changes here, but ``chainlink #183`` has its own dedicated PR (#341). payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: fix(loop-detector): sliding-window catches A,B,A,B alternation (chainlink #183)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Correct fix for the alternation-bypass. Pre-fix the detector only compared the latest message to its immediate predecessor, so A,B,A,B reset the streak on every other send. The new sliding-window via `deque(maxlen=window_size)` computes `max(similarity) over all messages in window` — second A finds the first A, streak increments as expected.

Test coverage is right where I'd want it: explicit A,B,A,B,A test that verifies the streak progression, plus a window-size boundary test that pins the eviction behavior (A → fillers → A with window_size=2 should NOT match). Existing 10 tests still pass — confirms no false positives on non-repeating, dissimilar, identical-repeat, or normalization paths.

Minor observation (non-blocking): an A,B,A,C near-miss case isn't explicitly tested, but the 0.9 similarity threshold should keep false positives rare in practice. Closes chainlink #183. Approve.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: fix(rate-limits): atomic write + threading.Lock to prevent file corruption (chainlink #181)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Solid fix. Concurrent writes to `<home>/.mimir/rate_limits.json` had two failure modes — a TOCTOU race on read-modify-write, and a non-atomic `Path.write_text` that could leave partial content on a crash. The fix addresses both: `threading.Lock` serializes the full read-modify-write cycle, and `_write_json_atomic()` uses `tempfile.mkstemp` + `os.replace` so the file is never half-written.

Test quality is what makes this approve-rather-than-approve-with-nits. `test_record_sync_concurrent_threads_no_corruption` actually fires 4 threads × 50 writes through `ThreadPoolExecutor` — that's a real stress test, not just a "lock exists" check. Plus the survives-corrupt-existing-file test guards against the recovery path.

One small staleness in `record_sync()`'s docstring (still says "No async lock" — now true at the `threading` layer rather than `asyncio`) but the actual code + flow is correct. Closes chainlink #181. Approve.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: fix(budget): quota_recovered silently dropped from asyncio.to_thread (chainlink #184)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Clean fix for the documented diagnosis. `asyncio.to_thread()` runs the callable on a thread that has no event loop, so `get_running_loop()` raised + the `quota_recovered` event silently vanished. The fix correctly captures the main loop before entering the thread and bridges back via `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe()`. Fall-back path for direct-async callers (no event_loop kwarg) preserves existing test behavior.

Tests cover both paths: unit test mocking the threadsafe submission + an integration test that actually runs through `asyncio.to_thread()` and asserts `quota_recovered` lands in the event log. Both explicitly trigger the lazy-expiry condition (5min stale pause) so the failure mode is exercised end-to-end.

Closes chainlink #184 cleanly. Approve.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.title: fix(saga): move PRAGMA foreign_keys toggle out of executescript (chainlink #186)

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
LGTM — clean fix for the documented SQLite-PRAGMA-inside-executescript gotcha.

### What's right

- **Diagnosis is correct.** `executescript` issues an implicit `COMMIT` and runs the DDL inside a transaction; `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON/OFF` requires being outside any transaction, so the in-DDL PRAGMAs were silently no-ops. The v6 migration only worked by accident (SQLite happens not to enforce FK on `DROP TABLE` / `RENAME` DDL).
- **Fix is in the right place.** Connection-level `conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF")` / `=ON` around the `executescript` call, with the migration DDL strings cleaned of the dead PRAGMA statements. The wrap fires per-migration in the loop — slightly wasteful for v2/v3/v4 that don't need FK=OFF, but the cost is negligible and the uniform pattern is easier to maintain.
- **Tests cover both directions.** `test_apply_pending_migrations_restores_fk_on_after_each_migration` pins the post-state. `test_migration_ddl_strings_contain_no_pragma_foreign_keys` pins that no future migration accidentally re-introduces the no-op pattern — with comment-stripping so the explanatory note in v6's DDL doesn't false-positive.
- **Closes chainlink #186** + the pre-OSS review's notable-bugs item #7 sub-point (PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON inside executescript transaction is a no-op) cleanly. That entry can be marked resolved.

### One minor doc nit (non-blocking)

`test_apply_pending_migrations_restores_fk_on_after_each_migration` docstring says:
> Because PRAGMA cannot be read from within executescript, we check the post-migration connection state via a separate conn.execute().

PRAGMA can be **read** inside executescript (it's a query). The restriction is that connection-state-modifying PRAGMAs (including `foreign_keys=`) can't be **set** while a transaction is active. Doc-only — the test setup is correct regardless.

Approving. Good catch + clean execution from a self-spawned heartbeat investigation.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: feat(scaffold-docker): --mode=pypi for image-build PyPI installs (closes #332)

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Overview

Clean two-shape design that threads `mode` through `render_dockerfile`, `render_compose_yml`, `render_start_sh`, and `scaffold()` with full backward-compatibility. The defensive `userdel`/`groupdel` block solves the real 1Password build failure, and test coverage is thorough (13 new tests, regression guards for workspace mode).

One concrete bug to fix before merge — the rest are nits.

---

## 🐛 Bug: `{MIMIR_EXTRAS}` placeholder collides with `${MIMIR_EXTRAS}` Docker ARG reference

In `_DOCKERFILE_BASE_PYPI`:

```dockerfile
ARG MIMIR_EXTRAS="{MIMIR_EXTRAS}"
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip \
 && pip install --no-cache-dir "mimir-agent[${MIMIR_EXTRAS}]"
```

`render_dockerfile` does:
```python
base = base.replace("{MIMIR_EXTRAS}", extras_csv)
```

`str.replace` is substring-based, so it replaces `{MIMIR_EXTRAS}` everywhere it appears — including inside `${MIMIR_EXTRAS}` on the `pip install` line. With `extras_csv = "anthropic,discord,slack,mcp"`, the generated Dockerfile has:

```dockerfile
ARG MIMIR_EXTRAS="anthropic,discord,slack,mcp"   # ✓ correct
RUN pip install ... "mimir-agent[$anthropic,discord,slack,mcp]"  # ✗ broken
```

The shell expands `$anthropic` to empty string; Docker builds silently produce an image where `pip install` installs `mimir-agent[,discord,slack,mcp]` — an invalid extras spec that'll fail at build time. The tests miss this because `test_render_dockerfile_pypi_mode_installs_from_pypi` only checks for the prefix `pip install --no-cache-dir "mimir-agent["`, not that `${MIMIR_EXTRAS}` survived intact.

**Fix:** use a placeholder that can't appear inside a shell `${VAR}` reference. Two options:

Option A — different marker:
```python
# In template: ARG MIMIR_EXTRAS="__MIMIR_EXTRAS__"
base = base.replace("__MIMIR_EXTRAS__", extras_csv)
```

Option B — escape the shell ref in the template using `${{MIMIR_EXTRAS}}` (double braces), which Python's `.replace` won't touch, then unfold if needed. But Option A is simpler and consistent with how other templates in this file avoid the collision.

Add a test that asserts `'${MIMIR_EXTRAS}' in out` (or `'"mimir-agent[${MIMIR_EXTRAS}]"' in out`) after substitution to lock this in.

---

## Nits

**`ScaffoldMode = str` type alias** — fine for documentation, but `Literal["workspace", "pypi"]` gives mypy-checkable exhaustion without the overhead of an enum. Not blocking, since `_MODES` + argparse `choices` enforce it at the CLI boundary and `scaffold()` validates it in-code.

**Duplicate userdel block** — both `_DOCKERFILE_BASE` and `_DOCKERFILE_BASE_PYPI` contain the identical 10-line defensive `RUN existing_uid_user=...` block. A named constant (`_USERDEL_BLOCK`) would prevent the two from drifting if the logic needs updating. Low risk today, drift risk as templates grow.

**`userdel 2>/dev/null || true`** — swallows errors silently. If `userdel` fails for an unexpected reason (locked user, running process), the build continues and the subsequent `useradd` will still fail with exit code 4 — but now the error from `userdel` is gone. Consider logging a warning instead of full suppression:
```bash
userdel "$existing_uid_user" || echo "[Dockerfile] WARNING: userdel failed — useradd may also fail"
```

**`fastembed` pre-warm `|| true`** — intentional and documented; just confirming this is expected behavior for offline builds.

---

## What's solid

- Back-compat default (`workspace`) is exactly right — silent mode switch on existing homes would be bad.
- The `_FRAGMENTS_SENTINEL` partition approach applies cleanly to both templates; no sentinel duplication.
- PyPI `start.sh` is properly minimal — git auth + `mimir setup` + `exec mimir run`, no boot-time source fetch.
- gitignore allowlist for deployment infrastructure is the right call: these files belong in source control for disaster recovery.
- Mode validation at three layers (argparse `choices`, `scaffold()` guard, `render_*` else-raises) is defense-in-depth.
- `test_render_dockerfile_includes_

**Bug fix (MIMIR_EXTRAS collision)** — `__MIMIR_EXTRAS__` is the right choice: double-underscore can't appear inside `${VAR}`, so the str.replace is safe. The inline comment on `render_dockerfile` explains the why precisely. Regression test `test_render_dockerfile_pypi_preserves_shell_extras_ref` pins both ends of the invariant — the shell ref survives, the ARG default is set, no stray `$anthropic` artifact.

**Nit: ScaffoldMode alias** — `Literal["workspace", "pypi"]` gives mypy exhaustion-checking at the type boundary. ✓

**Nit: shared userdel block** — `_USERDEL_BLOCK` constant extracted as a single-quote block with no Python placeholders; both templates inline via `__USERDEL_BLOCK__`. The drift hazard is gone. ✓

**Nit: userdel error logging** — now emits `WARNING: userdel $existing_uid_user failed — subsequent useradd may also fail` instead of swallowing. ✓

Test coverage is thorough: 13 new test functions covering pypi mode (Dockerfile, compose.yml, start.sh, end-to-end scaffold), regression guards for workspace mode, parametrized userdel test across both modes. Ready to merge.

The fix detects any non-mimir user at the target UID/GID and deletes it before the \`useradd\`. Applied to BOTH the workspace and PyPI templates so neither shape regresses.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.body:
Addressed all 4 items from the review (\`7ff337a\`):

**Bug — \`{MIMIR_EXTRAS}\` placeholder collision** — fixed. Swapped to \`__MIMIR_EXTRAS__\` (double-underscore marker can't appear inside \`\${VAR}\`). Regression test \`test_render_dockerfile_pypi_preserves_shell_extras_ref\` pins both ends: \`\${MIMIR_EXTRAS}\` survives intact in the pip-install line, no \`\$<extras-name>\` artifacts in the output.

**Nit 1 — \`Literal["workspace", "pypi"]\`** — done. Type alias is now mypy-checkable; \`_MODES\` narrowed accordingly.

**Nit 2 — DRY userdel block** — extracted \`_USERDEL_BLOCK\` constant. Both templates inline it via \`base.replace("__USERDEL_BLOCK__", _USERDEL_BLOCK)\`. Side effect: the userdel becomes its own \`RUN\` step (separate layer) — accepted trade-off for one DRY source-of-truth.

**Nit 3 — \`userdel \|\| true\` → log warning** — done. Failures now print a clear \`[Dockerfile] WARNING:\` line explaining that the subsequent useradd may also fail, so the operator sees the upstream reason instead of just the downstream symptom.

Confirmed the \`fastembed || true\` is intentional and documented.

Full suite: **2778 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed**.

Ready for re-review.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: fix: drop [claude-code] extra — PyPI rejects packages with direct URL deps

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Overview

Necessary blocker-fix for the v0.1.0 PyPI publish. The root cause is real and the fix shape is correct — PyPI genuinely rejects `Requires-Dist` entries with `git+` URLs, even behind optional extras. Dropping `[claude-code]` / `[dev-claude-code]` and routing to a separate install step is the right call given that upstream patches (#2/#4/#6) haven't landed yet.

## What's solid

- **Lock file cleanup is complete** — `langchain-claude-code`, `claude-agent-sdk`, and the entire `dev-claude-code` resolved group are all correctly removed from `uv.lock`. No orphaned refs.
- **Dockerfile parameterization** — `LANGCHAIN_CLAUDE_CODE_REF` as a build arg is the right shape. SHA is a single source of truth at the Dockerfile layer; bumping is one-arg override without editing the file.
- **`allow-direct-references` removal** — consistent with dropping all direct refs. Correct.
- **Documentation** — README is honest about the temporary nature of the workaround and cross-references #268 for restoration. The "after merge" re-tag procedure in the PR body is a nice ops note.
- **Tests** — 2762 passed / 0 failed. Clean.

## One real concern: SHA is hardcoded in 3 non-Dockerfile places

`f7af15b613d1e016437740f739321316730cdd39` appears in:

| File | Context |
|------|---------|
| `README.md` | Quickstart install snippet |
| `README.md` | Development section snippet |
| `mimir/agent.py` | `ImportError` message body |

The Dockerfile has `LANGCHAIN_CLAUDE_CODE_REF` as a build arg — good. But the Python `ImportError` and both README snippets are raw literals. When the SHA bumps (which #268 tracks), `agent.py` is non-obvious to update and easy to miss. A developer who hits the ImportError and follows the message will install the stale SHA.

**Suggestion (not a blocker for this PR):** pull the SHA into a single constant in agent.py (`_LANGCHAIN_CLAUDE_CODE_REF = "f7af15b..."`) and reference it from the ImportError string, then keep the README in sync. Or file a chainlink sub-task on #268 to "update SHA in README + agent.py when pin bumps" so it doesn't fall through the cracks.

## Minor nits

- The `ImportError` message is now a 5-part string concatenation across 6 lines. It works, but if you're touching it again for the SHA update, folding into a single triple-quoted string or a `textwrap.dedent` block would be cleaner.
- `README.md` quickstart comment: `#   Anthropic Max plan (free):   one extra install step — see "Claude Max plan" below` — the indentation alignment with the lines above is slightly off (extra spaces vs the other comment lines). Cosmetic only.

## Verdict

**Approve.** Fix is correct, test suite is clean, lock file is fully reconciled. SHA drift across README + ImportError is worth a follow-up but doesn't block the publish.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
Clean, well-scoped pre-OSS doc pass. The tier structure in the PR description is a good audit shape — tier-by-tier reasoning makes the intent clear and will serve as a changelog reference.

## What's correct

**README split** — two-block shape (PyPI canonical / dev clone) is exactly right. The extras table gives new operators a decision tree without requiring them to understand the full dependency graph first. Reordering auth options (API key first, Max plan second) is correct: Max plan now requires the `claude-code` extra, so it's no longer zero-config.

**SPEC.md Dockerfile** — updated snippet accurately reflects the live Dockerfile shipped in PR #331: user-owned venv at `/home/mimir/venv`, `pip install mimir-agent[${MIMIR_EXTRAS}]`, `git` added to OS deps (needed since `langchain-claude-code` is git-pinned). Removing the `uv` install layer and the `COPY --chown` source-copy lines is correct for a PyPI-install shape.

**reflect.md `$MIMIR_HOME`** — env-var expansion is the right abstraction here. Shell heredocs in these code blocks are instructions to the agent, not rendered template substitutions, so the `$MIMIR_HOME` in the `wc -l` and `mv` commands expands correctly at run-time (mimir always has `MIMIR_HOME` set). The `$(date +%Y-W%V)` inside double-quotes still expands correctly — no quoting problem.

**identity-lookup rewrite** — `uv run --extra dev python <<'PY'` → `python <<'PY'` with the `'PY'` single-quoting preserved is exactly right: single-quote heredoc prevents bash from expanding the `$` variables inside the Python body, while `python` without the uv preamble works in any environment where mimir is installed. The contextual reword ("work regardless of how mimir was installed" / "any Python process that has `mimir` importable") is more precise than the previous workspace-locked framing.

**github SKILL.md** — "when `cwd` is inside a git checkout of the target repo" + "from the local `origin`" is a cleaner explanation of what `gh` actually does internally.

## Minor notes (non-blocking)

- The extras table groups `anthropic`, `openai`, and `codex-plus` together as "model adapter packages" without separate rows. Fine for now, but `codex-plus` is likely less well-known — a one-liner parenthetical ("Codex Plus gateway") would help future operators scanning the table.
- `uv sync --extra dev` in the development block has a comment `# or [dev-claude-code] for the Claude Code subprocess path` — but `uv sync --extra dev-claude-code` isn't standard uv syntax (extras are `--extra <name>`). Assuming this is a shorthand comment rather than literal syntax, but might trip up a reader who tries it verbatim. Could clarify as `uv sync --extra dev-claude-code` (explicit) or drop to a prose note.
- The bench-runner clarification ("benches require the `[bench]` extra and aren't part of the PyPI install") is correct and helpful. Worth confirming `[bench]` is actually a declared extra in `pyproject.toml` — if it's `[benchmarks]` or similar, the docs would mismatch.

## Verification

The grep-based verification in the PR description is a solid completeness check. The test results (2755 passed, 0 failed) confirm no runtime regressions from the template/skill changes.

Approving — the tier-structured cleanup is exactly what pre-OSS docs need.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: fix(update_on_start): drain startup events into events.jsonl + Dockerfile WORKDIR

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Review: fix(update_on_start): drain startup events into events.jsonl + Dockerfile WORKDIR

**Approve.** This cleanly resolves the real bug I flagged in the PR #330 review — the two-stage write/drain pattern is the right shape for the pre-init constraint. Tests are comprehensive. A few notes below.

---

### What this does right

- **Correct invariant**: sidecar lives in the bind-mounted `<home>/.mimir/` so it survives the `os.execv` that runs immediately after a successful install. The new process picks it up in `_on_startup` after `init_logger` is up. The lifecycle is sound.
- **Best-effort everywhere**: both `_record_startup_event` and `consume_startup_events` catch `OSError`/`Exception`, log a warning, and continue. The stdout path is still the in-process diagnostic; the sidecar is the persistence path. Neither blocks the other.
- **`ts` stripping before replay**: correct — the event logger stamps its own timestamp; replaying the pre-init one would produce confusing timestamps in `events.jsonl`.
- **Test coverage**: all five cases I'd want — happy path, failure path, drain-and-delete, no-sidecar noop, malformed-line robustness.
- **`_make_emit` factory**: clean encapsulation; callers don't need to remember both paths.

---

### Minor observations (non-blocking)

**1. Stale sidecar if `unlink()` fails**

If `consume_startup_events` drains successfully but `sidecar.unlink()` raises (full disk, weird FS state), the sidecar survives. On the next restart, `_record_startup_event` *appends* to it rather than truncating, so the next drain replays the old events again plus the new ones. Consequence: duplicate `mimir_update_applied` / `_failed` events in `events.jsonl` — cosmetic, not a correctness issue. If you want to harden this, truncate the sidecar at the *start* of `apply_pending_update` (before writing) rather than relying on drain-side unlink, but I wouldn't block the PR on it.

**2. Missing type annotation on `async_log_event`**

```python
async def consume_startup_events(home: Path, async_log_event) -> int:
```

Could be `Callable[..., Awaitable[int]]` or just `AsyncLogEvent = Callable[..., Coroutine[Any, Any, None]]`. Minor — doesn't affect runtime behavior.

**3. Tests import underscore-prefixed internals**

```python
from mimir.update_on_start import (
    _record_startup_event,
    _STARTUP_EVENTS_BASENAME,
    consume_startup_events,
)
```

Acceptable and common in Python test suites — the underscore convention signals "internal, test at your own risk." Worth a quick comment in the test file so future readers know this is intentional rather than an oversight.

**4. Dockerfile ordering** — correct as written. `useradd -m` already created `/home/mimir` owned by `mimir`; `WORKDIR` after `USER` doesn't change ownership but lands in the right directory. No action needed.

---

### Summary

The fix is correct, the tests cover the important paths, and the two-stage write/drain pattern handles the pre-init constraint elegantly. The items above are all non-blocking observations. Ship it.

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Follow-up commit review (c28d5415 — "fix: address mimir-carreira review nits on #333")

The prior approval at 182bf3ba stands. This follow-up commit cleanly addresses the two items I flagged:

### What changed

**`_truncate_startup_events` (new function)**
Exactly right. Called from `apply_pending_update` immediately after confirming a flag is present, before any sidecar writes — so a stale sidecar from a prior boot (drain succeeded but `unlink()` failed) gets cleared before the current boot appends its events. The `FileNotFoundError` pass-through is correct (normal case), the `OSError` warning path is correct (best-effort, doesn't abort). 

One cosmetic note: "truncate" conventionally means set-size-to-zero while "unlink" removes the file. The docstring says "Clear" which is accurate; the function name is a mild misnomer. Not worth a change at this point, just worth knowing for future readers.

**Type annotation on `consume_startup_events`**
`async_log_event: Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]` is correct. Better than untyped; callers and type-checkers can now verify the signature.

**Two new tests**
- `test_apply_truncates_stale_sidecar_before_writing` — pins the exact edge case (prior-boot stale entry absent from drain). Well-shaped: plants stale sentinel, runs apply, asserts "STALE" not in specs AND current-boot events ARE present.
- `test_apply_does_not_touch_sidecar_when_no_flag` — pins the invariant that `_truncate_startup_events` doesn't fire on the no-flag code path. Correct and minimal.

**Test comment in `test_consume_startup_events_drains_into_async_logger`**
Added rationale for importing underscore-prefixed internals — good documentation hygiene.

### Verdict

Approved. All nits addressed, no new issues introduced, test suite clean (2760 passed per PR description). Good to merge for v0.1.0.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: feat(docker): install mimir-agent from PyPI; support pending-update flag

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Review: feat(docker): install mimir-agent from PyPI; support pending-update flag

**Overall: approve.** Clean, well-reasoned rework. The PyPI install + user-owned venv is the right shape for the pending-update flow, the documentation inside the Dockerfile is excellent, and removing `uv` from the image is a clear win. PR #330 is now merged, so the dependency is satisfied.

---

### What's good

- **User-owned venv placement** — `/home/mimir/venv` owned by the mimir user is exactly right for `pip install --upgrade` from `update_on_start.py` without root escalation.
- **Build-arg `MIMIR_EXTRAS`** — sensible default (`anthropic,discord,slack,mcp`), overridable at build time. The comment block listing available extras is a useful reference.
- **`git` dep correctly explained** — the `langchain-claude-code` git-pin rationale (chainlink #268) is spelled out inline; easy to audit and eventually remove.
- **Auto-update comment block** — the 5-step flow description is exactly the right level of detail for an operator reading the Dockerfile cold.
- **`|| true` on setup/fastembed** — retained correctly; both steps are best-effort at image-build time.
- **`--no-cache-dir` on pip** — correct; Docker layer caching is more reliable than pip's own cache, and you don't want a stale pip cache leaking between image rebuilds.

---

### Minor notes (no blockers)

**1. No WORKDIR set after `USER mimir`**

The old Dockerfile set `WORKDIR /home/mimir/app`; nothing replaces it here. Container shells land at `/`. Not a bug — Docker defaults to `/` — but operators who `docker exec -it <container> bash` will get a slightly confusing starting location. Consider:
```dockerfile
WORKDIR /home/mimir
```
or use `/home/mimir/agent` (same as MIMIR_HOME) if you want a predictable landing point.

**2. No `MIMIR_VERSION` build-arg**

`pip install mimir-agent[...]` without a version pin means `docker build` always resolves to latest. That's probably intentional (operators build and get latest at build time; the pending-update flow handles in-place upgrades), but it does mean the image isn't reproducible from the same Dockerfile. If that ever matters:
```dockerfile
ARG MIMIR_VERSION=">=0.1.0"
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir "mimir-agent[${MIMIR_EXTRAS}]${MIMIR_VERSION}"
```
Not a blocker — just worth a conscious decision.

**3. Dockerfile won't build until v0.1.0 publishes**

PR description calls this out explicitly ("Both PRs need to land before the v0.1.0 tag push"), so it's deliberate. Just confirming the ordering is documented, which it is. Once the tag pushes and the OIDC publish workflow fires, `mimir-agent 0.1.0` will be available and `docker build` will work.

**4. Carry-over: `update_on_start.py` logging gap from #330**

I flagged in the #330 review that algedonic events from the update flow won't reach `events.jsonl` because `init_logger()` hasn't been called yet when `update_on_start.py` runs. That bug is now in the codebase and this PR depends on it. Worth a follow-up chainlink if one isn't already filed — doesn't block this PR.

---

Approve. The PyPI install flow is the right long-term direction, and the Dockerfile reads clearly enough that an operator unfamiliar with the pending-update design can follow it.

payload.author: jasoncarreira
payload.title: feat: pending-update flag — operator-approved auto-install on restart

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Overview

Solid design that threads the right needle between full-autonomy (risky) and operator-shells-in (friction). The tri-zone framing is appropriate — the flag file is the consent signal, the agent can write it but only after explicit operator approval. Design rationale in `update_on_start.py` is thorough and well-organized; `_exec` injection seam for testing is exactly right.

## Significant concern: algedonic events won't reach `events.jsonl`

The PR description promises:

> On the first turn after restart, `mimir_update_applied` (positive) or `mimir_update_failed` (negative) lands in the algedonic block.

But the current implementation doesn't deliver this. In `server.py`, `apply_pending_update` is called before `asyncio.run()` and before `init_logger(...)`. The `log_event` argument defaults to `_default_log_event`, which calls `log.info(...)` on the module logger — but at this point `logging.basicConfig` hasn't run yet, so the root logger has no handlers and the message goes nowhere. After `os.execv`, the new process boots fresh with no memory of the event.

**Result:** `mimir_update_applied` and `mimir_update_failed` are registered in `_EVENT_RULES` and have rendering in `_render_event_line`, but they'll never appear in the per-turn feedback block because they never reach `events.jsonl`.

**Suggested fix:** Before the `exec_fn(...)` call (and before returning on failure), write a small "outcome" file — e.g., `.mimir/pending-update-outcome.json` — with the event kind and fields. Then in the `run()` coroutine, after `init_logger` is called, check for and consume this file via `await log_event(...)`. This mirrors the flag-file pattern already established and fires the event from a fully-initialized logger.

This is worth a follow-up fix before the update flow gets operator-visible use.

## Minor observations

**`os.getcwd()` fallback in `server.py`:** 
```python
_home_for_flag = Path(os.environ.get("MIMIR_HOME") or os.getcwd())
```
If the process starts from an unexpected cwd (e.g., `/`), the `.mimir/` directory gets created in the wrong place and the flag is silently missed. A `log.warning` when falling back to cwd would help.

**No `target_version` format validation:** The version string goes directly into the pip spec (`mimir-agent==<value>`). No shell injection risk since subprocess is called with a list, and pip would reject a malformed spec cleanly — but a simple `re.match(r'^[\w.+-]+$', target_version)` check in `write_flag` would catch typos before they persist to disk.

**`FileNotFoundError` path in `_run_pip_install` not tested:** The timeout case has a test; the `FileNotFoundError` (Python not on PATH) case is handled in the code but missing from `test_update_on_start.py`. Minor — the path is realistic enough to warrant coverage.

**`uv.lock` rename (`mimir` → `mimir-agent`) in `dev-claude-code` marker:** This looks like a straggler from the PyPI rename, not directly related to the pending-update feature. Fine to bundle but worth a note in the commit message.

## What works well

- `PendingUpdate` frozen dataclass is clean; `_read_flag` tolerating empty/malformed JSON is the right defensive posture (bare `touch` as approval is a nice UX affordance for operator manual override)
- `subprocess.run` with list argv (not `shell=True`) is correct; `capture_output=True` prevents pip output from flooding server stdout
- Flag deletion on BOTH success and failure (loop avoidance) is the right default; the comment explains why
- `os.execv` over exit-and-supervisor-restart is the right call; rationale in the docstring is clear
- 22 tests covering the module and tool, including injection seams for subprocess and exec — good coverage of the failure paths
- `pytest.importorskip("saga.benchmarks")` fix is the right pattern; matches the existing precedent in the langchain-code-patches test

Approving. The algedonic-event gap is the one thing worth closing before this feature gets real operator use — the rest is solid.

payload.title: feat: PyPI publish workflow + fix runtime/bench dep split

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
Both fixes are correct and the PR is well-documented. Approving with a couple of minor nits.

## pyproject.toml — dep split

The root issue is right: `saga` is a workspace member, not a PyPI package, so it must not appear in base `[project.dependencies]`. Moving it to an `[bench]` optional extra is the correct fix. The comment block explaining _why_ (`mimir/saga/` is the runtime memory backend that ships in the wheel; top-level `saga` is the bench harness only) is exactly what future readers need.

`dev-claude-code` self-reference (`mimir[dev,claude-code]` → `mimir-agent[dev,claude-code]`) is a latent bug from PR #326; glad this caught it before a first release attempt.

## publish.yml

Workflow structure is solid:
- Two-job split (build then publish via artifact hand-off) is the standard pypa pattern and keeps the OIDC permission scoped to the publish job only — `id-token: write` is on `publish`, not global. Good.
- OIDC trusted publishing over stored API tokens is the right call for a new project: no secret rotation, auditability via the OIDC claim.
- `workflow_dispatch` trigger is handy for dry-run builds (will build fine, might fail on publish if PyPI publisher isn't configured yet — acceptable).

**Nit 1 — action SHA pinning.** `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1` and `astral-sh/setup-uv@v3` use mutable floating tags. For a publish workflow (where a compromised action could inject a malicious wheel), SHA pinning is worth doing:

```yaml
uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@76f52bc884231f62b9a034ebfe128415bbaabdfc  # release/v1 as of 2026-05
uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@f0ec1fc3b38f5e7cd731bb6ce540c5af426746bb  # v3
```

Not a blocker for initial release, but good hygiene before making the repo widely visible.

**Nit 2 — `uv build --no-sources`.** The CI build step uses plain `uv build`. Adding `--no-sources` would enforce that the sdist/wheel is built as if no local workspace sources exist — a useful sanity check that confirms the wheel doesn't accidentally depend on anything local-only. Since `saga` is now optional, this would pass cleanly and give extra confidence.

Neither nit is a blocker. The dep split is the real fix and it's correct.

payload.title: fix(saga): FAISS dim from provider on fresh DB + close chainlink #175 migration trap

payload.author: mimir-carreira
payload.body:
## Summary

Two clean fixes in one PR: the FAISS dim mismatch on fresh DB (pre-OSS item #14) and the schema migration footgun from chainlink #175. Both are well-motivated, well-tested, and mirror patterns already established in the codebase.

## FAISS dim fix (`_ensure_index`)

The hardcoded `dim=1024` fallback was a silent correctness hazard for any non-Voyage provider — the FAISS index would build at 1024 while the embeddings table stored vectors at the provider's actual dim (384, 1536, 3072), causing every incremental add to silently drop. The fix mirrors exactly what `_ensure_sessions_index` already does: ask the provider for `dimensions()` when the table is empty. Resolution order (constructor arg → DB row → provider → None/FTS-only) is correct.

The `_index_built = True` cache on the provider-unavailable path is right — prevents repeated failed lookups on a genuinely empty DB. The broad `except Exception` is appropriate given it's a graceful degradation path; the comment explains it well.

## Schema migration fix (`_detect_schema_version` + `_apply_pending_migrations`)

The PRAGMA-introspection approach correctly distinguishes all the cases:

- Fresh DB via `schema.sql` (`fresh=True`) → stamp target and return (unchanged)
- Half-init retry (v6 tables, empty schema_version) → FK marker fires, stamp v1..v6, no migrations loop
- True pre-migration-era DB (no sessions table) → returns v1, applies v2..N
- v2/v3/v4 detection via sessions table column inspection → correct and idempotent

One non-blocking observation: the `except sqlite3.OperationalError` around `PRAGMA foreign_key_list(access_events)` is defensive but technically unnecessary — SQLite's PRAGMA returns empty rows for non-existent tables rather than raising. Harmless either way.

## Tests

17 targeted tests pass (7 new FAISS dim cases + 10 correctness regression cases incl. 3 new schema detection tests + xfail removed). Full suite: **2684 passed, 4 skipped** — clean.
